   393	
   394	We define a special class of measurements that are relevant to the soundness
   395	properties of the low-degree test.
   396	
   397	\begin{definition}[Low-degree polynomial measurements]
   398	  \label{def:ld-meas}
   399	  Define $\polymeas{m}{d}{q}$ to be the set of POVM measurements whose outcomes
   400	  correspond to (individual) degree-$d$ polynomials of $m$ variables over
   401	  $\F_q$.
   402	  More generally, for an integer $\ldc$ and tuples $m=(m_1, m_2, \ldots,
   403	  m_\ldc)$, $d=(d_1, d_2, \ldots, d_\ldc)$ and $q=(q_1, q_2, \ldots, q_\ldc)$,
   404	  we let $\simulpolymeas{m}{d}{q}{\ldc}$ be the set of measurements $G =
   405	  \{G_{g_1,\, g_2,\, \ldots\,,\, g_\ldc}\}$ such that for $i\in\{1, 2, \ldots,
   406	  \ldc\}$, $g_i$ is a polynomial $g_i:\F_{q_i}^{m_i} \rightarrow
   407	  \F_{q_i}$ with individual degree $d_i$ (see \Cref{sec:ld-encoding} for a definition of individual degree). 
   408	\end{definition}
   409	
   410	Quantum soundness of a version of the classical low-degree test for polynomials of low \emph{total} degree was claimed
   411	in~\cite{natarajan2018low}, building on an analysis of a three-prover version of the test in~\cite{vidick2016three}. Unfortunately there is a gap in the soundness analysis of this test. For our construction we use the low individual degree test, whose quantum soundness is shown in~\cite{ML20} and generalized in~\cite{ji2021quantum}. We state the result in the form that is most directly useful for us, and show how the stated result follows from~\cite{ji2021quantum}.
   412	
   413	\begin{theorem}[Quantum soundness of the simultaneous classical low-degree test]
   414	  \label{lem:ld-soundness}
   415	  There exists a function $\delta_{\ld}(\eps, q, m, d, \ldc) = a (dm \ldc)^a (\eps^b + q^{-b} + 2^{-bmd})$ for universal constants $a\geq 1$ and $0<b\leq 1$ 
   416	such that the following
   417	  holds.
   418	  For all $\eps > 0$ and parameter tuple $\ldparams = (q, m, d, \ldc)$, for all
   419	  projective strategies $(\psi,A,B)$ that succeed with probability at least
   420	  $1-\eps$ in the game $\game^\ld_\ldparams$, there exists measurements
   421	  \[G^w \in \simulpolymeas{m}{d}{q}{\ldc}\] on $\mH_w$, for
   422	  $w\in\{\alice,\bob\}$, such that
   423	  \begin{equation*}
   424	    \begin{split}
   425	      A^{\Point,\, u}_{a_1,\, a_2,\, \ldots\,,\, a_\ldc}
   426	      & \abc[\delta_{\ld}]
   427	      G^\bob_{[(g_1(u),g_2(u),\ldots,g_\ldc(u)) = (a_1,\, a_2,\, \ldots \,,\, a_\ldc)]}\;,\\
   428	      G^\alice_{[(g_1(u),g_2(u),\ldots,g_\ldc(u)) = (a_1,\, a_2,\, \ldots \,,\, a_\ldc)]}
   429	      & \abc[\delta_{\ld}]
   430				 B^{\Point,\, u}_{a_1,\, a_2,\, \ldots\,,\, a_\ldc}\;,\\
   431	      G^\alice_{g_1,\, g_2,\, \ldots \,,\, g_\ldc}
   432	      & \abc[\delta_{\ld}]
   433	      G^\bob_{g_1,\, g_2,\, \ldots \,,\, g_\ldc}\;,
   434	    \end{split}
   435	  \end{equation*}
   436	  where $\delta_{\ld} = \delta_{\ld}(\eps, q, m, d, \ldc)$, 
   437	  and all three statements are with respect to the state $\ket{\psi}$.
   438	In addition, the first two approximations hold under the uniform distribution over $u\in \F_q^m$,
   439		whereas there is no question distribution associated with the third approximation.
   440	\end{theorem}
   441	
   442	\begin{proof}
   443	Let $\ldparams = (q, m, d, \ldc)$
   444	where $m, d, \ldc \in \N$ are integers, $q \in \N$ is an admissible field size,
   445	and $m$ divides $q$. Let $\Sigma=\F_q$. Let $\code \subseteq \Sigma^q$ be the Reed-Solomon code with degree $d$. Explicitly, $\code$ is the set of all $(p(x_1),\ldots,p(x_n))$ where $p:\F_q\to\F_q$ is a univariate polynomial of degree at most $d$ and $x_1,\ldots,x_n$ are an enumeration of $\F_q$. Then in the (standard) notation from~\cite{ji2021quantum} $\code$ is a linear $[q,d+1,n-d+1]_\Sigma$ code.
   446	
   447	Observe that the two-prover tensor code test, for the code $\code^{\otimes m}$, as described in~\cite[Figure 1 and Figure 2]{ji2021quantum}, is identical to the game $\game^\ld$ with parameters $\ldparams$ and $\ldc=1$, whose decider is presented in Figure~\ref{fig:ld-decider}. This is because 
   448	\begin{enumerate}
   449	\item The \emph{axis-parallel line-versus-point test} from Figure~\ref{fig:ld-decider} is identical to the \emph{axis-parallel lines test} from~\cite[Figure 1]{ji2021quantum}, with the only difference that in Figure~\ref{fig:ld-decider} the roles of A and B are chosen uniformly at random. This is consistent with the two-prover variant of the tensor code test from~\cite[Section 4.1]{ji2021quantum}.
   450	\item The \emph{diagonal line-versus-point test} from Figure~\ref{fig:ld-decider} is identical to the \emph{subcube commutation test} from~\cite[Figure 1]{ji2021quantum}, with again the added symmetrization between players. 
   451	\item The \emph{consistency test} from Figure~\ref{fig:ld-decider} is identical to the \emph{synchronicity test} from~\cite[Figure 2]{ji2021quantum}.
   452	\end{enumerate}
   453	
   454	As a result,~\cite[Theorem 4.7]{ji2021quantum}, in which we choose the parameter $k$ as $k=m^3d$,  immediately yields \Cref{lem:ld-soundness}.
   455	
   456	To conclude it remains to extend the result to the case of general $\ldc$. This is done 
   457	via a standard reduction, following exactly the same steps as the derivation of Theorem 4.43 from Theorem 4.40 in~\cite{NW19}.
   458	\end{proof}

   465	\subsubsection{Complexity of the classical low-degree test.}
   466	The CL functions and decision procedure of the low-degree test are incorporated
   467	as subroutines in some of the normal form verifiers constructed in subsequent
   468	sections.
   469	The next lemma establishes the time complexity of these procedures as a function
   470	of the parameter tuple $\ldparams = (q,m,d,k)$.
   471	The lemma also establishes the time complexity of computing the {description} of
   472	the decision procedure $\decider^\ld$ as a Turing machine, given the parameter
   473	tuple $\ldparams$ as input.

155	\begin{notation}\label{not:conditioned-on-last-direction}
   156	Our proof will be via induction,
   157	i.e.\ proving soundness of the $(m+1,q,d)$-low individual degree test
   158	using the soundness of the $(m,q,d)$-low individual degree test.
   159	To do this, we will frequently use the axis-parallel line test in the specific case of $i = m+1$.
   160	Thus, it will be convenient to introduce the following notation.
   161	Let $(\psi, A, B, L)$ be a symmetric strategy for the $(m+1, q, d)$-low individual degree test,
   162	Then for each $u \in \F_q^m$ we will write $B^u_f$ as shorthand for $B^{\ell}_f$,
   163	where $\ell = \{(u, x) \mid x \in \F_q\}$.
   164	For a function $f:\ell \rightarrow \F_q$,
   165	we will also sometimes write $f(x)$ as shorthand for $f(u,x)$.
   166	\end{notation}
   167	
   168	\begin{definition}
   169	Consider the $(m,q,d)$-low individual degree test.
   170	For $j \in \{1, \ldots, m\}$,
   171	we refer to the \emph{$j$-restricted diagonal lines test}
   172	as the diagonal lines test conditioned on $\bi = j$.
   173	For example, in the $m$-restricted diagonal lines test,
   174	the line $\bell$ is simply a uniformly random line in $\F_q^m$.
   175	\end{definition}
   176	
   177	Now we state our main theorem using notation which will be introduced in \Cref{sec:prelims} below.
   178	This the formal version of \Cref{thm:main-informal}.
   179	
   180	\begin{theorem}[Main theorem; quantum soundness of the low individual degree test]\label{thm:main-formal}
   181	  Consider a projective strategy $(\psi, A^{\mathrm{A}},B^{\mathrm{A}},L^{\mathrm{A}},A^{\mathrm{B}},B^{\mathrm{B}},L^{\mathrm{B}})$ 
   182	   which passes the  $(m,q,d)$-low individual degree test with probability at least $1-\eps$.
   183	  Let $k \geq md$ be an integer.
   184	  Let
   185	  \begin{equation*}
   186	  \nu = 100000 k^2m^4 \cdot \Big(\eps^{1/40000} + (d/q)^{1/40000} + e^{-k/(2560000m^2)}\Big).
   187	  \end{equation*}
   188	Then there exists projective measurements $G^{\mathrm{A}}, G^{\mathrm{B}} \in \polymeas{m}{q}{d}$ with the following properties:
   189	\begin{enumerate}
   190	  \item (Consistency with~$A$):  On average over $\bu \sim \F_q^{m}$,
   191		  \begin{align*}
   192		  A^{\mathrm{A},u}_a \otimes I
   193		  	&\simeq_{\nu} I \otimes G^{\mathrm{B}}_{[g(u)=a]},\\
   194		I \otimes A^{\mathrm{B},u}_a
   195		  	&\simeq_{\nu}  G^{\mathrm{A}}_{[g(u)=a]} \ot I.
   196		  \end{align*}
   197	\item (Self-consistency):
   198		\begin{equation*}
   199		G^{\mathrm{A}}_g \ot I \simeq_{\nu} I \ot G^{\mathrm{B}}_g.
   200		\end{equation*}
   201	\end{enumerate}
   202	\end{theorem}
   203	
   204	We note that there is a tradeoff in \Cref{thm:main-formal} specified by the parameter~$k$.
   205	As~$k$ increases, $\nu$'s prefactor $k^2$ increases.
   206	On the other hand, as $k$ increases, the term $e^{- k/(2560000m^2)}$ which also occurs in $\nu$ \emph{decreases}.
   207	Thus, when applying this theorem, one must select~$k$ to balance these competing demands.
   208	Typically, choosing $k = \poly(m)$ should be more than sufficient for applications.
   209	We believe that this parameter~$k$ is an artifact of our proof,
   210	and we hope that it will be removed in the future.

    59	\section{Key theorem forms}
    60	
    61	Throughout, $q = 2^k$ with $k$ odd is an admissible field size, the tuple
    62	$(q,m,d)$ is admissible when moreover $d \ge 1$ and $m \mid q$, and
    63	$\mathrm{ideg}_{d,m}(\F_q)$ denotes the $m$-variate polynomial representatives
    64	over $\F_q$ of individual degree at most $d$.  The comparison involves four
    65	theorem forms.
    66	\begin{enumerate}
    67	  \item \textbf{Source theorem form} (the polynomial-pair measurement).  There
    68	  is a function $\delta_S(\eps,m,d,q) = a(md)^a(\eps^b + q^{-b} + 2^{-bmd})$,
    69	  for universal constants $a > 1$ and $0 < b < 1$, such that for every
    70	  admissible $(q,m,d)$ and every projective strategy for the Pauli basis test
    71	  succeeding with probability at least $1-\eps$, there is a projective
    72	  measurement $\{\hat S_{g_X,g_Z}\}$ with outcomes pairs of polynomials in
    73	  $\mathrm{ideg}_{d,m}(\F_q)$ whose evaluations are $\delta_S$-consistent, on
    74	  average over a uniform point $u \in \F_q^m$ and in both bases
    75	  $W \in \{X,Z\}$, with the corresponding points measurements
    76	  $\{\hat M^{(\mathrm{Point},W),u}_a\}$ of the strategy, together with the
    77	  symmetric counterpart of this relation.
    78	  \item \textbf{Missing instantiation obligation.}  The classical low
    79	  individual degree game with parameter tuple $(q,\, 2m+2,\, d,\, 1)$ is well
    80	  defined, and the combined point and line measurements assembled in the
    81	  analysis constitute a strategy for it of value at least
    82	  $1 - \delta_{\mathrm{combine}}$.  The game's question distribution draws
    83	  its axis and diagonal indices through an index function
    84	  $\chi_{2m+2}\colon \F_q \to \{1,\ldots,2m+2\}$ with classes of equal size
    85	  $q/(2m+2)$, so the game exists only when $2m+2$ divides $q$.
    86	  \item \textbf{Restricted form supported by the present route.}  The source
    87	  theorem form under the additional hypothesis $2m+2 \mid q$.  Among
    88	  admissible tuples this hypothesis holds exactly when $m = 1$ and
    89	  $q \ge 8$; it fails for every admissible tuple with $m \ge 2$ and for
    90	  $(q,m) = (2,1)$.
    91	  \item \textbf{Repaired import form} (recommended target).  Quantum
    92	  soundness of the directly indexed variant of the classical low individual
    93	  degree game over $\F_q^{m'}$, for every dimension $m' \ge 1$ and
    94	  admissible $q$, with no divisibility hypothesis: the question
    95	  distribution samples the axis index, and the diagonal prefix index,
    96	  uniformly from $\{1,\ldots,m'\}$ directly rather than through an index
    97	  function on $\F_q$, and line questions carry the sampled index itself in
    98	  place of the seed $s \in \F_q$; the error is
    99	  $\delta_{\mathrm{ld}}(\eps,q,m',d,k) = a(dm'k)^a(\eps^b + q^{-b} +
   100	  2^{-bm'd})$.  This is a candidate target form, not an established one:
   101	  proving it carries the same two import obligations as the $\chi$-based
   102	  import (Section~\ref{sec:import-obligations}), and deriving the present
   103	  form from it when $m' \mid q$ requires the strategy transport described
   104	  under the candidate repairs below, whose synchronicity step is an open
   105	  obligation.
   106	\end{enumerate}

   108	\section{The source assertion and the obstruction}
   109	
   110	We examine the final step of the subsection ``Applying the classical
   111	low-degree test'' in the analysis of the Pauli basis test in the compression
   112	paper of Ji, Natarajan, Vidick, Wright, and Yuen (MIP$^{*}$=RE,
   113	arXiv:2001.04383), whose quantum soundness component builds on the low
   114	individual degree test of \cite{Ji2020LowIndividualDegree}.%
   115	\footnote{Tracked in \localissue{0002}.  In the mirror of the source
   116	consulted here, the polynomial-pair lemma and its proof are at
   117	\path{references/qpbt-paper/14_analysis_of_the_pauli_basis_test.tex},
   118	lines~1267--1288; the sub-line lemma is at lines~1063--1116 and the combined
   119	line lemma at lines~1020--1034 of the same file.  The game parametrization
   120	with its divisibility, the index function, the soundness statement with its
   121	proof, and admissibility are at
   122	\path{references/qpbt-paper/08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex},
   123	lines~33--35, 214--219, 413--458, and 958--961.}
   124	There, the combined point measurements
   125	$\{\hat Q^{x,z,\alpha,\beta}_c\}$ and combined line measurements
   126	$\{\hat Q^{\ell}_f\}$, indexed by points of $\F_q^{2m+2}$ and lines in
   127	$\F_q^{2m+2}$, are asserted to form a strategy for the classical low
   128	individual degree game with parameters
   129	\[
   130	  \mathsf{ldparams} = (q,\, 2m+2,\, d,\, 1)
   131	  \tag{\path{lem:qld-4-7}}
   132	\]
   133	of value $1 - \delta_{\mathrm{combine}}$, and the quantum soundness theorem
   134	for that game is applied to produce the global polynomial-pair measurement.
   135	The two lemmas feeding this step are stated for the line-point distribution
   136	over $\F_q^{2m+2}$.
   137	
   138	The game, however, is parametrized by tuples $(q,m',d,k)$ with $q$ an
   139	admissible field size \emph{and $m'$ dividing $q$}.  The divisibility is not
   140	incidental: the question distribution is a conditionally linear distribution
   141	in which a uniform seed coordinate $s \in \F_q$, read as an integer in
   142	$\{0,\ldots,q-1\}$, determines the axis or diagonal index through the unique
   143	$\chi(s)$ with
   144	\[
   145	  s = (\chi(s)-1)\,\frac{q}{m'} + r, \qquad 0 \le r < \frac{q}{m'},
   146	  \tag{\path{eq:chi-func}}
   147	\]
   148	so that the $m'$ classes $\chi^{-1}(i)$ partition $\F_q$ into sets of equal
   149	size $q/m'$ and the index is uniform.  For $m' \nmid q$ neither the index
   150	function nor the line-point distribution built from it is defined.
   151	
   152	Admissibility of $(q,m,d)$ supplies only $m \mid q$.  Since an admissible $q$
   153	is a power of two, $m \mid q$ forces $m = 2^j$.  For $j \ge 1$ the integer
   154	$m+1 \ge 3$ is odd, so $2m+2 = 2(m+1)$ has an odd factor exceeding $1$ and
   155	divides no power of two; for $m = 1$ the condition $4 \mid q$ holds for every
   156	admissible $q$ except $q = 2$.  Thus the instantiation at dimension $2m+2$ is
   157	undefined for every admissible tuple with $m \ge 2$: for instance
   158	$(q,m,d) = (8,2,1)$ is admissible, while $6 \nmid 8$.  The source performs
   159	the instantiation without addressing the divisibility, so its proof route
   160	establishes the polynomial-pair lemma, and with it the soundness theorem for
   161	the Pauli basis test that rests on it, only for $m = 1$ and $q \ge 8$.
   162	
   163	\section{What the cited soundness theorem requires: the import obligations}
   164	\label{sec:import-obligations}
   165	
   166	The quantum soundness theorem for the classical game inherits the constraint
   167	$m' \mid q$ solely because it is stated for the game just described; its
   168	proof fixes an admissible $q$ with $m' \mid q$, asserts that the game with
   169	simultaneity parameter $1$ is \emph{identical} to the two-prover tensor-code
   170	test for the Reed--Solomon tensor code $\mathcal C^{\ot m'}$ of the same
   171	authors' \emph{Quantum soundness of testing tensor codes} (arXiv:2111.08131)
   172	\cite{Ji2021Quantum}, and concludes by Theorem~4.7 there, instantiated with
   173	that theorem's auxiliary integer parameter --- denoted $k$ in that source,
   174	and written $K$ here to avoid clashing with the field exponent and the
   175	simultaneity parameter --- chosen as $(m')^3 d$.  Neither
   176	the asserted identity nor the instantiation is complete as stated, so the
   177	import carries two verification obligations, which this section details and
   178	which the blueprint's proof node for the soundness statement records as
   179	open.  Both obligations are independent of the divisibility question: they
   180	arise at every dimension, for the $\chi$-based game where it is defined and
   181	equally for the directly indexed variant proposed under the candidate
   182	repairs.
   183	
   184	\paragraph{The cited test.}
   185	In the two-prover tensor-code test (Figures~1 and~2 of
   186	\cite{Ji2021Quantum}; the two-prover strategy format and the goodness
   187	measure are Definitions~4.5 and~4.6 there), the referee performs one of
   188	three subtests with probability $1/3$ each, assigning the two roles of each
   189	subtest to the two provers uniformly at random.  \emph{Axis-parallel lines
   190	test}: sample a uniform point $u \in [n]^{m'}$ and a uniform axis
   191	$j \in \{1,\ldots,m'\}$; send the axis-parallel line $\ell$ through $u$ in
   192	direction $j$ to one prover, who answers a codeword $g \in \mathcal C$;
   193	send $u$ to the other, who answers a field value $a$; accept iff
   194	$g(u_j) = a$.  \emph{Subcube commutation test}: sample

    12	The low-degree game used by the Pauli-basis combining argument is needed in
    13	dimension `2 * m + 2`.  The existing conditionally linear game represents a
    14	coordinate index by an equally sized fiber in the scalar field and therefore
    15	requires the dimension to divide the field size.  This file gives the separate
    16	directly indexed variant which samples that index directly.
    17	
    18	The geometric line carrier records the sampled coordinate, and line evaluation
    19	uses an `Option` outcome rather than assigning a value when a point does not
    20	determine one.  The game retains the point, axis-line, and diagonal-line answer
    21	formats and the nine ordered type branches of the original low-degree game.
    22	
    23	The `Transport` modules relate the direct game to the seed-indexed game and to
    24	the mature low individual degree test interface: `Transport.Correspondence`
    25	identifies coordinates, answers, and the question law of the two QPBT
    26	presentations; `Transport.SeedFiber` dilates a seed-indexed strategy to a
    27	direct strategy by a correlated residue register, and `Transport.SeedFiberValue`
    28	shows that the dilation preserves the value exactly; `Transport.Questions`
    29	reads mature lines as canonical direct questions and rebases direct answers;
    30	`Transport.Strategy` reads one coordinate of a projective direct strategy as a
    31	mature `ProjStrat`, with exact Born-weight formulas for both adapters; and
    32	`Transport.BranchComparison`, `Transport.DiagonalRecursion`, and
    33	`Transport.PassConversion` convert a value bound of the direct game into the
    34	pass hypothesis of the mature low individual degree theorem for every
    35	coordinate strategy.  `GameValue` supplies the rejection calculus relating the
    36	direct value to the mature branch weights.  `Transport.Error` carries the
    37	scalar half of the transport: the auxiliary sampling parameter with which
    38	the mature theorem is applied, bounds on the three terms of its error
    39	function, and the absorption of the resulting simultaneous-measurement
    40	estimate into the error function of `lem:ld-soundness`.
    41	`Transport.Consistency` identifies polynomial outcomes and transports the
    42	three mature consistency conclusions to the direct game.
    43	
    44	## References
    45	
    46	The underlying game is `def:ld-game` in
    47	`blueprint/src/chapter/ch13_qpbt_test.tex:17-105`, with source origin
    48	`references/qpbt-paper/08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:31-391`.
    49	The need for the directly indexed repair in Chapter 15 is explained around
    50	`rem:qld-4-7-divisibility` in
    51	`blueprint/src/chapter/ch15_qpbt_combining.tex:1257-1293` and in
    52	`docs/paper-gaps/qpbt_ld-dimension-divisibility.tex`.
    53	-/

    27	/-- Coefficient lists for a univariate polynomial of degree at most `c` in the
    28	direct scalar field. -/
    29	abbrev DirectDegPoly (D : DirectLdParams) (c : ℕ) :=
    30	  Fin (c + 1) → DirectScalarQ D
    31	
    32	/-- A direct line polynomial evaluates to `a` at `u` when `u` lies on the line
    33	and every parameter presenting `u` gives value `a`.  The universal clause
    34	keeps the zero-direction case explicit. -/
    35	def DirectEvaluatesTo {D : DirectLdParams} {c : ℕ} (line : DirectLineDesc D)
    36	    (f : DirectDegPoly D c) (u : Fin D.m → DirectScalarQ D)
    37	    (a : DirectScalarQ D) : Prop :=
    38	  (∃ t : DirectScalarQ D, u = line.base + t • line.direction) ∧
    39	    ∀ t : DirectScalarQ D, u = line.base + t • line.direction →
    40	      evalCoefficient f t = a
    41	
    42	/-- Option-completed evaluation of a direct line polynomial.  `none` is an
    43	explicit outcome when the point does not determine an evaluation; no field
    44	value is used as a fallback. -/
    45	noncomputable def directEvalOpt {D : DirectLdParams} {c : ℕ}
    46	    (line : DirectLineDesc D) (u : Fin D.m → DirectScalarQ D)
    47	    (f : DirectDegPoly D c) : Option (DirectScalarQ D) := by
    48	  classical
    49	  exact if h : ∃ a : DirectScalarQ D, DirectEvaluatesTo line f u a then
    50	    some (Classical.choose h)
    51	  else none
    52	
    53	/-- The typed question alphabet of the directly indexed game. -/
    54	abbrev DirectLdQuestion (D : DirectLdParams) := LdType × DirectLdSpace D
    55	
    56	/-- Canonicalize a common direct sample for one question type.  Irrelevant
    57	coordinates are fixed, so point questions reveal no sampled line index and
    58	axis-line questions reveal no diagonal direction. -/
    59	noncomputable def directLdMap (D : DirectLdParams) :
    60	    LdType → DirectLdSpace D → DirectLdSpace D
    61	  | .point, sample => ⟨sample.point, D.firstIndex, 0⟩
    62	  | .aline, sample =>
    63	      let direction := coordinateDirection sample.index
    64	      ⟨lineRepMap direction sample.point, sample.index, 0⟩
    65	  | .dline, sample =>
    66	      let direction := directPrefixProjection sample.index sample.direction
    67	      ⟨lineRepMap direction sample.point, sample.index, direction⟩
    68	
    69	/-- The directly indexed question distribution.  It has the same uniform
    70	ordered type-pair branches as `ldQuestionDistribution`, but its common sample
    71	contains an actual coordinate index rather than a field seed. -/
    72	noncomputable def directLdQuestionDistribution (D : DirectLdParams) :
    73	    Distribution (DirectLdQuestion D × DirectLdQuestion D) :=
    74	  (uniformDistribution ((LdType × LdType) × DirectLdSpace D)).map fun sample =>
    75	    ((sample.1.1, directLdMap D sample.1.1 sample.2),
    76	      (sample.1.2, directLdMap D sample.1.2 sample.2))

    78	/-- The directly indexed question law is probabilistic. -/
    79	theorem directLdQuestionDistribution_isProbability (D : DirectLdParams) :
    80	    (directLdQuestionDistribution D).IsProbability := by
    81	  exact (uniformDistribution_isProbability
    82	    ((LdType × LdType) × DirectLdSpace D)).map _

    85	inductive DirectLdAnswer (D : DirectLdParams) where
    86	  | pointVals (a : Fin D.k → DirectScalarQ D)
    87	  | alinePolys (a : Fin D.k → Fin (D.d + 1) → DirectScalarQ D)
    88	  | dlinePolys (a : Fin D.k → Fin (D.m * D.d + 1) → DirectScalarQ D)

    92	abbrev DirectLdAnswerCode (D : DirectLdParams) :=

    94	    ((Fin D.k → Fin (D.d + 1) → DirectScalarQ D) ⊕
    95	      (Fin D.k → Fin (D.m * D.d + 1) → DirectScalarQ D))

    28	
    29	/-- Relabel a matrix measurement along an equivalence of outcome alphabets. -/
    30	noncomputable def matrixMeasurementTransport
    31	    {alpha beta iota : Type*}
    32	    [Fintype alpha] [Fintype beta] [Fintype iota] [DecidableEq iota]
    33	    (e : alpha ≃ beta) (M : MIPStarRE.Quantum.Measurement alpha iota) :
    34	    MIPStarRE.Quantum.Measurement beta iota :=
    35	  MIPStarRE.Quantum.Measurement.ofSumEqOne
    36	    (fun b => M.effect (e.symm b))
    37	    (fun b => M.pos (e.symm b))
    38	    (by
    39	      calc
    40	        ∑ b, M.effect (e.symm b) = ∑ a, M.effect a :=
    41	          Equiv.sum_comp e.symm M.effect
    42	        _ = 1 := M.sum_eq_one)
    43	
    44	@[simp] theorem matrixMeasurementTransport_effect
    45	    {alpha beta iota : Type*}
    46	    [Fintype alpha] [Fintype beta] [Fintype iota] [DecidableEq iota]
    47	    (e : alpha ≃ beta) (M : MIPStarRE.Quantum.Measurement alpha iota)
    48	    (b : beta) :

    52	/-- Relabeling a projective matrix measurement preserves projectivity. -/
    53	theorem matrixMeasurementTransport_isProjective
    54	    {alpha beta iota : Type*}
    55	    [Fintype alpha] [Fintype beta] [Fintype iota] [DecidableEq iota]
    56	    (e : alpha ≃ beta) (M : MIPStarRE.Quantum.Measurement alpha iota)
    57	    (hM : MIPStarRE.QPBT.Measurement.IsProjective M) :
    58	    MIPStarRE.QPBT.Measurement.IsProjective (matrixMeasurementTransport e M) :=
    59	  fun b => hM (e.symm b)

    61	/-- Assemble a family of matrix measurements as diagonal blocks indexed by a
    62	finite classical register. -/
    63	noncomputable def blockDiagonalMeasurement
    64	    {alpha iota block : Type*}
    65	    [Fintype alpha] [Fintype iota] [DecidableEq iota]
    66	    [Fintype block] [DecidableEq block]
    67	    (M : block → MIPStarRE.Quantum.Measurement alpha iota) :
    68	    MIPStarRE.Quantum.Measurement alpha (iota × block) :=
    69	  MIPStarRE.Quantum.Measurement.ofSumEqOne
    70	    (fun a => Matrix.blockDiagonal fun r => (M r).effect a)
    71	    (fun a => Matrix.blockDiagonal_nonneg
    72	      (fun r => (M r).effect a) (fun r => (M r).pos a))
    73	    (by
    74	      ext ⟨i, r⟩ ⟨j, s⟩
    75	      simp only [Matrix.sum_apply, Matrix.blockDiagonal_apply]
    76	      by_cases hrs : r = s
    77	      · subst s
    78	        simp only [if_pos]
    79	        calc
    80	          ∑ x, (M r).effect x i j = (1 : Matrix iota iota ℂ) i j :=
    81	            by
    82	              simpa only [Matrix.sum_apply] using
    83	                congrFun (congrFun (M r).sum_eq_one i) j
    84	          _ = (1 : Matrix (iota × block) (iota × block) ℂ)
    85	              (i, r) (j, r) := by
    86	                change (if i = j then 1 else 0) =
    87	                  (if (i, r) = (j, r) then 1 else 0)
    88	                simp
    89	      · simp [hrs])

    92	    {alpha iota block : Type*}
    93	    [Fintype alpha] [Fintype iota] [DecidableEq iota]
    94	    [Fintype block] [DecidableEq block]
    95	    (M : block → MIPStarRE.Quantum.Measurement alpha iota)
    96	    (a : alpha) :
    97	    (blockDiagonalMeasurement M).effect a =
    98	      Matrix.blockDiagonal (fun r => (M r).effect a) :=

   101	/-- A block-diagonal family of projective measurements is projective. -/
   102	theorem blockDiagonalMeasurement_isProjective
   103	    {alpha iota block : Type*}
   104	    [Fintype alpha] [Fintype iota] [DecidableEq iota]
   105	    [Fintype block] [DecidableEq block]
   106	    (M : block → MIPStarRE.Quantum.Measurement alpha iota)
   107	    (hM : ∀ r, MIPStarRE.QPBT.Measurement.IsProjective (M r)) :
   108	    MIPStarRE.QPBT.Measurement.IsProjective (blockDiagonalMeasurement M) := by
   109	  intro a
   110	  constructor
   111	  · change Matrix.blockDiagonal (fun r => (M r).effect a) *
   112	        Matrix.blockDiagonal (fun r => (M r).effect a) =
   113	      Matrix.blockDiagonal (fun r => (M r).effect a)
   114	    rw [← Matrix.blockDiagonal_mul]
   115	    congr 1
   116	    funext r
   117	    exact (hM r a).isIdempotentElem.eq
   118	  · change (Matrix.blockDiagonal (fun r => (M r).effect a))ᴴ =
   119	      Matrix.blockDiagonal (fun r => (M r).effect a)
   120	    rw [Matrix.blockDiagonal_conjTranspose]
   121	    congr 1
   122	    funext r
   123	    exact (hM r a).isSelfAdjoint.star_eq

   125	/-! ## The correlated residue state -/
   126	
   127	/-- The normalized maximally correlated state on the common seed-fiber
   128	residue. -/
   129	noncomputable def seedResidueAncilla (L : LdParams) :
   130	    EuclideanSpace ℂ
   131	      (Fin (L.q / L.m) × Fin (L.q / L.m)) := by
   132	  letI : Nonempty (Fin (L.q / L.m)) :=
   133	    Fin.pos_iff_nonempty.mp L.seedFiberCard_pos
   134	  exact eprState (Fin (L.q / L.m))
   135	
   136	/-- The seed-residue ancilla has unit norm. -/
   137	theorem seedResidueAncilla_norm (L : LdParams) :
   138	    ‖seedResidueAncilla L‖ = 1 := by
   139	  letI : Nonempty (Fin (L.q / L.m)) :=
   140	    Fin.pos_iff_nonempty.mp L.seedFiberCard_pos
   141	  exact eprState_norm (Fin (L.q / L.m))
   142	
   143	/-- Reindexing Euclidean coordinates along an equivalence preserves norm. -/
   144	theorem reindexState_norm_eq
   145	    {iota kappa : Type*}
   146	    [Fintype iota] [DecidableEq iota]
   147	    [Fintype kappa] [DecidableEq kappa]
   148	    (e : iota ≃ kappa) (psi : EuclideanSpace ℂ iota) :
   149	    ‖reindexState e psi‖ = ‖psi‖ := by
   150	  rw [← sq_eq_sq₀ (norm_nonneg _) (norm_nonneg _)]
   151	  rw [EuclideanSpace.norm_sq_eq, EuclideanSpace.norm_sq_eq]
   152	  change (∑ j : kappa, ‖psi (e.symm j)‖ ^ 2) = ∑ i : iota, ‖psi i‖ ^ 2
   153	  exact e.symm.sum_comp (fun i => ‖psi i‖ ^ 2)
   154	
   155	/-- The coordinate tensor of two Euclidean vectors has the product norm. -/
   156	theorem vecTensor_norm_eq
   157	    {iota kappa : Type*}
   158	    [Fintype iota] [DecidableEq iota]
   159	    [Fintype kappa] [DecidableEq kappa]
   160	    (u : EuclideanSpace ℂ iota) (v : EuclideanSpace ℂ kappa) :
   161	    ‖vecTensor u v‖ = ‖u‖ * ‖v‖ := by
   162	  rw [← sq_eq_sq₀ (norm_nonneg _) (mul_nonneg (norm_nonneg _) (norm_nonneg _))]
   163	  rw [EuclideanSpace.norm_sq_eq, mul_pow, EuclideanSpace.norm_sq_eq,
   164	    EuclideanSpace.norm_sq_eq]
   165	  change (∑ p : iota × kappa, ‖u p.1 * v p.2‖ ^ 2) =
   166	    (∑ i : iota, ‖u i‖ ^ 2) * ∑ j : kappa, ‖v j‖ ^ 2
   167	  simp only [norm_mul, mul_pow]
   168	  rw [← Finset.univ_product_univ, Finset.sum_product, Finset.sum_mul]
   169	  apply Finset.sum_congr rfl
   170	  intro i hi
   171	  rw [Finset.mul_sum]
   172	
   173	/-- Tensor the original strategy state with the maximally correlated residue
   174	state and shuffle the factors back into the two local carriers. -/
   175	noncomputable def seedFiberLiftedState
   176	    {G : Game} (S : Strategy G) (L : LdParams) :
   177	    EuclideanSpace ℂ
   178	      ((S.ιA × Fin (L.q / L.m)) × (S.ιB × Fin (L.q / L.m))) :=
   179	  reindexState prodShuffle (vecTensor S.ψ (seedResidueAncilla L))
   180	
   181	/-- The correlated seed-fiber lift preserves normalization of the strategy
   182	state. -/
   183	theorem seedFiberLiftedState_norm
   184	    {G : Game} (S : Strategy G) (L : LdParams) :
   185	    ‖seedFiberLiftedState S L‖ = 1 := by
   186	  rw [seedFiberLiftedState, reindexState_norm_eq, vecTensor_norm_eq,
   187	    S.ψ_norm, seedResidueAncilla_norm, one_mul]
   188	
   189	/-! ## From the seed-indexed game to the direct game -/
   190	
   191	/-- The seed-indexed question selected in one residue block of a direct
   192	question.  Applying `ldCL` ensures that irrelevant ambient coordinates are
   193	canonicalized exactly as in the source game. -/
   194	noncomputable def seededLdQuestion (L : LdParams)
   195	    (q : DirectLdQuestion L.toDirectLdParams)
   196	    (residue : Fin (L.q / L.m)) : LdQuestion L :=
   197	  (q.1, ldCL L q.1 (ldSpaceOfDirectResidue L q.2 residue))
   198	
   199	/-- Dilate a strategy for the seed-indexed low-degree game to the directly
   200	indexed game.  The two local carriers receive correlated copies of the seed
   201	residue, and each measurement is block diagonal in that residue. -/
   202	noncomputable def ldStrategyToDirect (L : LdParams)
   203	    (S : Strategy (ldGame L)) : Strategy (directLdGame L.toDirectLdParams) where
   204	  ιA := S.ιA × Fin (L.q / L.m)
   205	  ιB := S.ιB × Fin (L.q / L.m)
   206	  ψ := seedFiberLiftedState S L
   207	  ψ_norm := seedFiberLiftedState_norm S L
   208	  A q := blockDiagonalMeasurement fun residue =>
   209	    matrixMeasurementTransport (ldDirectAnswerEquiv L)
   210	      (S.A (seededLdQuestion L q residue))
   211	  B q := blockDiagonalMeasurement fun residue =>
   212	    matrixMeasurementTransport (ldDirectAnswerEquiv L)
   213	      (S.B (seededLdQuestion L q residue))
   214	
   215	/-- Projectivity is preserved by the correlated seed-fiber dilation. -/
   216	theorem ldStrategyToDirect_isProjective (L : LdParams)
   217	    (S : Strategy (ldGame L)) (hS : S.IsProjective) :
   218	    (ldStrategyToDirect L S).IsProjective := by
   219	  constructor
   220	  · intro q
   221	    apply blockDiagonalMeasurement_isProjective
   222	    intro residue
   223	    apply matrixMeasurementTransport_isProjective
   224	    exact hS.1 (seededLdQuestion L q residue)
   225	  · intro q
   226	    apply blockDiagonalMeasurement_isProjective
   227	    intro residue
   228	    apply matrixMeasurementTransport_isProjective
   229	    exact hS.2 (seededLdQuestion L q residue)
   230	
   231	@[simp] theorem ldStrategyToDirect_A_effect (L : LdParams)
   232	    (S : Strategy (ldGame L))
   233	    (q : DirectLdQuestion L.toDirectLdParams)
   234	    (answer : DirectLdAnswer L.toDirectLdParams) :
   235	    ((ldStrategyToDirect L S).A q).effect answer =
   236	      Matrix.blockDiagonal fun residue =>
   237	        (S.A (seededLdQuestion L q residue)).effect
   238	          ((ldDirectAnswerEquiv L).symm answer) :=
   239	  rfl
   240	
   241	@[simp] theorem ldStrategyToDirect_B_effect (L : LdParams)
   242	    (S : Strategy (ldGame L))
   243	    (q : DirectLdQuestion L.toDirectLdParams)
   244	    (answer : DirectLdAnswer L.toDirectLdParams) :
   245	    ((ldStrategyToDirect L S).B q).effect answer =
   246	      Matrix.blockDiagonal fun residue =>
   247	        (S.B (seededLdQuestion L q residue)).effect
   248	          ((ldDirectAnswerEquiv L).symm answer) :=
   249	  rfl

    11	## References
    12	
    13	The line-point distributions originate in
    14	`references/qpbt-paper/08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:243-272`.
    15	The directly indexed repair is documented in

    27	noncomputable section
    28	
    29	/-- Parameters for the directly indexed low-degree game.  Unlike `LdParams`,
    30	this directly indexed line-space construction has no divisibility field: its coordinate index is
    31	sampled from `Fin m` rather than encoded by fibers of `chiIndex`.
    32	
    33	This is the direct-index repair described in
    34	`docs/paper-gaps/qpbt_ld-dimension-divisibility.tex`; it is not a second
    35	definition of the source verifier game. -/

    37	  q : ℕ
    38	  m : ℕ
    39	  d : ℕ
    40	  k : ℕ
    41	  hm : 1 ≤ m
    42	  hd : 1 ≤ d

    44	  hq : IsAdmissibleSize q

    46	/-- The canonical scalar model for directly indexed parameters. -/
    47	noncomputable def DirectLdParams.model (D : DirectLdParams) : FixedFieldModel D.q :=
    48	  fixedFieldModel D.q D.hq

    50	/-- The scalar field of a directly indexed low-degree game. -/
    51	abbrev DirectScalarQ (D : DirectLdParams) := D.model.K

    53	/-- The first coordinate, available because directly indexed dimensions are
    54	positive. -/
    55	def DirectLdParams.firstIndex (D : DirectLdParams) : Fin D.m :=

   161	/-- Squared effects in one measurement fiber sum to at most the identity. -/
   162	private theorem measurement_fiber_sum_adjoint_mul_le_one {α β ι : Type*}
   163	    [Fintype α] [Fintype β] [Fintype ι] [DecidableEq ι]
   164	    (M : MIPStarRE.Quantum.Measurement (α × β) ι) (a : α) :
   165	    ∑ b : β, (M.effect (a, b))ᴴ * M.effect (a, b) ≤ 1 := by
   166	  classical
   167	  have hsquare_le (z : α × β) :
   168	      (M.effect z)ᴴ * M.effect z ≤ M.effect z := by
   169	    rw [measurement_effect_hermitian M z]
   170	    exact MIPStarRE.Quantum.sq_le_self (M.pos z) (measurement_effect_le_one M z)
   171	  calc
   172	    ∑ b : β, (M.effect (a, b))ᴴ * M.effect (a, b) ≤
   173	        ∑ b : β, M.effect (a, b) :=
   174	      Finset.sum_le_sum fun b _ => hsquare_le (a, b)
   175	    _ ≤ ∑ a' : α, ∑ b : β, M.effect (a', b) :=
   176	      Finset.single_le_sum
   177	        (fun a' _ => Finset.sum_nonneg fun b _ => M.pos (a', b))
   178	        (Finset.mem_univ a)
   179	    _ = ∑ z : α × β, M.effect z := (Fintype.sum_prod_type _).symm
   180	    _ = 1 := M.sum_eq_one

/-- Squared effects in one measurement fiber sum to at most the identity. -/
private theorem measurement_fiber_sum_adjoint_mul_le_one {α β ι : Type*}
    [Fintype α] [Fintype β] [Fintype ι] [DecidableEq ι]
    (M : MIPStarRE.Quantum.Measurement (α × β) ι) (a : α) :
    ∑ b : β, (M.effect (a, b))ᴴ * M.effect (a, b) ≤ 1 := by
  classical
  have hsquare_le (z : α × β) :
      (M.effect z)ᴴ * M.effect z ≤ M.effect z := by
    rw [measurement_effect_hermitian M z]
    exact MIPStarRE.Quantum.sq_le_self (M.pos z) (measurement_effect_le_one M z)
  calc
    ∑ b : β, (M.effect (a, b))ᴴ * M.effect (a, b) ≤
        ∑ b : β, M.effect (a, b) :=
      Finset.sum_le_sum fun b _ => hsquare_le (a, b)
    _ ≤ ∑ a' : α, ∑ b : β, M.effect (a', b) :=
      Finset.single_le_sum
        (fun a' _ => Finset.sum_nonneg fun b _ => M.pos (a', b))
        (Finset.mem_univ a)
    _ = ∑ z : α × β, M.effect z := (Fintype.sum_prod_type _).symm
    _ = 1 := M.sum_eq_one

    (M : MIPStarRE.Quantum.Measurement (α × β) ιA) (a : α) :
    (1 - ∑ b : β, (leftTensor (ι₂ := ιB) (M.effect (a, b)))ᴴ *
      leftTensor (ι₂ := ιB) (M.effect (a, b))).PosSemidef := by
  apply Matrix.nonneg_iff_posSemidef.mp
  rw [sub_nonneg]
  calc
    ∑ b : β, (leftTensor (ι₂ := ιB) (M.effect (a, b)))ᴴ *
          leftTensor (ι₂ := ιB) (M.effect (a, b)) =
        ∑ b : β, leftTensor (ι₂ := ιB)
          ((M.effect (a, b))ᴴ * M.effect (a, b)) := by
      apply Finset.sum_congr rfl
      intro b _

    _ = leftTensor (ι₂ := ιB)

      leftTensor_finset_sum Finset.univ _
    _ ≤ leftTensor (ι₂ := ιB) (1 : Op ιA) :=
      leftTensor_mono (measurement_fiber_sum_adjoint_mul_le_one M a)

/-- A projective effect survives exactly in its postprocessing fiber. -/
private theorem postprocess_effect_mul_effect {ζ α ι : Type*}
    [Fintype ζ] [DecidableEq ζ] [Fintype α] [DecidableEq α]
    [Fintype ι] [DecidableEq ι]
    (M : MIPStarRE.Quantum.Measurement ζ ι)
    (hM : MIPStarRE.QPBT.Measurement.IsProjective M)
    (f : ζ → α) (b : α) (z : ζ) :
    (M.postprocess f).effect b * M.effect z =
      if f z = b then M.effect z else 0 := by
  classical
  rw [MIPStarRE.Quantum.Measurement.postprocess_effect, Finset.sum_mul]
  calc
    ∑ y ∈ Finset.univ.filter (fun y => f y = b), M.effect y * M.effect z =

          if y = z then M.effect z else 0 := by
      apply Finset.sum_congr rfl
      intro y _
      by_cases hyz : y = z
      · subst y
        rw [if_pos rfl]
        exact (hM z).isIdempotentElem.eq
      · rw [if_neg hyz]
        exact projective_effect_mul_effect_eq_zero M hM hyz
    _ = if f z = b then M.effect z else 0 := by simp

/-- Averaging over the product of two finite distributions is iterated
averaging. -/
theorem avgOver_distribution_prod {X Y : Type*}
    [DecidableEq X] [DecidableEq Y] (μ : Distribution X) (ν : Distribution Y)
    (f : X × Y → ℝ) :
    avgOver (Distribution.prod μ ν) f =
      avgOver μ (fun x => avgOver ν (fun y => f (x, y))) := by
  unfold avgOver
  change (∑ p ∈ μ.support.product ν.support,
    (μ.weight p.1 * ν.weight p.2) * f p) = _
  calc
    (∑ p ∈ μ.support.product ν.support,
        (μ.weight p.1 * ν.weight p.2) * f p) =
        ∑ x ∈ μ.support, ∑ y ∈ ν.support,
          (μ.weight x * ν.weight y) * f (x, y) := by
      exact Finset.sum_product' μ.support ν.support
        (fun x y => (μ.weight x * ν.weight y) * f (x, y))
    _ = _ := by
      apply Finset.sum_congr rfl
      intro x _
      rw [Finset.mul_sum]
      apply Finset.sum_congr rfl
      intro y _
      ring

/-- The diagonal overlap after a common relabeling is the sum over pairs of
original outcomes with equal labels. -/
theorem diagonal_postprocess_stateQForm_eq_pair_sum
    {α β ιA ιB : Type*} [Fintype α] [DecidableEq α]
    [Fintype β] [DecidableEq β]
    [Fintype ιA] [DecidableEq ιA] [Fintype ιB] [DecidableEq ιB]
    (A : Measurement α ιA) (B : Measurement α ιB)
    (ψ : EuclideanSpace ℂ (ιA × ιB)) (f : α → β) :
    (∑ b : β, stateQForm ψ
      (heteroKron ((A.postprocess f).effect b) ((B.postprocess f).effect b))) =
      ∑ a : α, ∑ a' : α, if f a = f a' then
        stateQForm ψ (heteroKron (A.effect a) (B.effect a')) else 0 := by
  classical
  have hterm (b : β) : stateQForm ψ
      (heteroKron ((A.postprocess f).effect b) ((B.postprocess f).effect b)) =
      ∑ a : α, ∑ a' : α, if f a = b ∧ f a' = b then
        stateQForm ψ (heteroKron (A.effect a) (B.effect a')) else 0 := by
    rw [MIPStarRE.Quantum.Measurement.postprocess_effect,
      MIPStarRE.Quantum.Measurement.postprocess_effect,
      heteroKron_finset_sum_left, stateQForm_finset_sum, Finset.sum_filter]
    apply Finset.sum_congr rfl
    intro a _
    by_cases hab : f a = b
    · rw [if_pos hab, heteroKron_finset_sum_right, stateQForm_finset_sum,
        Finset.sum_filter]
      apply Finset.sum_congr rfl
      intro a' _
      by_cases ha'b : f a' = b <;> simp [hab, ha'b]
    · simp [hab]
  simp_rw [hterm]
  rw [Finset.sum_comm]
  apply Finset.sum_congr rfl
  intro a _
  rw [Finset.sum_comm]
  apply Finset.sum_congr rfl
  intro a' _
  by_cases haa' : f a = f a'
  · rw [haa']
    simp
  · apply Eq.trans (Finset.sum_eq_zero (fun b _ => by
      simp only [ite_eq_right_iff]
      intro hpair
      exact (haa' (hpair.1.trans hpair.2.symm)).elim))
    simp [haa']

/-- The consistency defect of tensor-placed local measurements is the average
of their pointwise off-diagonal tensor overlap. -/
theorem consistencyDefect_placed_eq_avg_point
    {X α ιA ιB : Type*}
    [Fintype X] [DecidableEq X] [Fintype α] [DecidableEq α]
    [Fintype ιA] [DecidableEq ιA] [Fintype ιB] [DecidableEq ιB]
    (μ : Distribution X) (A : X → Measurement α ιA)
    (B : X → Measurement α ιB) (ψ : EuclideanSpace ℂ (ιA × ιB)) :
    consistencyDefect μ
        (fun x a => heteroKron ((A x).effect a) 1)
        (fun x a => heteroKron 1 ((B x).effect a)) ψ =
      avgOver μ (fun x => ∑ a : α, ∑ a' : α, if a = a' then 0 else
        stateQForm ψ (heteroKron ((A x).effect a) ((B x).effect a'))) := by
  unfold consistencyDefect
  apply avgOver_congr
  intro x
  apply Finset.sum_congr rfl
  intro a _
  apply Finset.sum_congr rfl
  intro a' _
  by_cases haa' : a = a'
  · simp [haa']
  · simp only [if_neg haa']
    rw [consistency_term_eq_stateQForm, placed_product_stateQForm_eq]

      ∑ r : R, stateQForm ψ

      (∑ g : Γ, stateQForm ψ (heteroKron (A.effect g) (B.effect g))) + ε := by

        intro g' _

+/-- Averaging over the product of two finite distributions is iterated
+averaging. -/
+theorem avgOver_distribution_prod {X Y : Type*}
+    [DecidableEq X] [DecidableEq Y] (μ : Distribution X) (ν : Distribution Y)
+    (f : X × Y → ℝ) :
+    avgOver (Distribution.prod μ ν) f =
+      avgOver μ (fun x => avgOver ν (fun y => f (x, y))) := by
+  unfold avgOver
+  change (∑ p ∈ μ.support.product ν.support,
+    (μ.weight p.1 * ν.weight p.2) * f p) = _
+  calc
+    (∑ p ∈ μ.support.product ν.support,
+        (μ.weight p.1 * ν.weight p.2) * f p) =
+        ∑ x ∈ μ.support, ∑ y ∈ ν.support,
+          (μ.weight x * ν.weight y) * f (x, y) := by
+      exact Finset.sum_product' μ.support ν.support
+        (fun x y => (μ.weight x * ν.weight y) * f (x, y))
+    _ = _ := by
+      apply Finset.sum_congr rfl
+      intro x _
+      rw [Finset.mul_sum]
+      apply Finset.sum_congr rfl
+      intro y _
+      ring

+      ∑ a : α, ∑ a' : α, if f a = f a' then
+        stateQForm ψ (heteroKron (A.effect a) (B.effect a')) else 0 := by
+  classical
+  have hterm (b : β) : stateQForm ψ
+      (heteroKron ((A.postprocess f).effect b) ((B.postprocess f).effect b)) =
+      ∑ a : α, ∑ a' : α, if f a = b ∧ f a' = b then
+        stateQForm ψ (heteroKron (A.effect a) (B.effect a')) else 0 := by

+    intro a _

+        Finset.sum_filter]
+      apply Finset.sum_congr rfl
+      intro a' _
+      by_cases ha'b : f a' = b <;> simp [hab, ha'b]
+    · simp [hab]
+  simp_rw [hterm]
+  rw [Finset.sum_comm]
+  apply Finset.sum_congr rfl
+  intro a _
+  rw [Finset.sum_comm]
+  apply Finset.sum_congr rfl
+  intro a' _
+  by_cases haa' : f a = f a'

+    simp

+      simp only [ite_eq_right_iff]
+      intro hpair
+      exact (haa' (hpair.1.trans hpair.2.symm)).elim))
+    simp [haa']

/-- The square root of the average squared operator distance satisfies the
ordinary triangle inequality. -/
theorem sqrt_opFamilyDistSq_triangle {X α ι : Type*}
    [Fintype α] [Fintype ι] [DecidableEq ι]
    (μ : Distribution X) (A B C : X → α → Op ι)
    (ψ : EuclideanSpace ℂ ι) :
    Real.sqrt (opFamilyDistSq μ A C ψ) ≤
      Real.sqrt (opFamilyDistSq μ A B ψ) +
        Real.sqrt (opFamilyDistSq μ B C ψ) := by
  let u : X → α → EuclideanSpace ℂ ι := fun x a =>
    applyOperatorToState (A x a - B x a) ψ
  let v : X → α → EuclideanSpace ℂ ι := fun x a =>
    applyOperatorToState (B x a - C x a) ψ
  have hpoint (x : X) (a : α) :
      ‖applyOperatorToState (A x a - C x a) ψ‖ ^ 2 ≤
        ‖u x a‖ ^ 2 + ‖v x a‖ ^ 2 + 2 * (‖u x a‖ * ‖v x a‖) := by
    have hdecomp : applyOperatorToState (A x a - C x a) ψ = u x a + v x a := by
      rw [show A x a - C x a = (A x a - B x a) + (B x a - C x a) by abel]
      simp only [u, v, applyOperatorToState, map_add, LinearMap.add_apply]
    rw [hdecomp]
    have hadd := norm_add_le (u x a) (v x a)
    nlinarith [norm_nonneg (u x a), norm_nonneg (v x a),
      norm_nonneg (u x a + v x a)]
  have hcross :
      avgOver μ (fun x => ∑ a : α, ‖u x a‖ * ‖v x a‖) ≤
        Real.sqrt (opFamilyDistSq μ A B ψ) *
          Real.sqrt (opFamilyDistSq μ B C ψ) := by
    calc
      avgOver μ (fun x => ∑ a : α, ‖u x a‖ * ‖v x a‖) ≤
          |avgOver μ (fun x => ∑ a : α, ‖u x a‖ * ‖v x a‖)| :=
        le_abs_self _
      _ ≤ Real.sqrt (avgOver μ (fun x => ∑ a : α, ‖u x a‖ ^ 2)) *
          Real.sqrt (avgOver μ (fun x => ∑ a : α, ‖v x a‖ ^ 2)) := by
        apply MIPStarRE.LDT.Preliminaries.weightedFinsetCauchySchwarz
        · intro x a
          simp only [abs_mul, abs_norm, Real.sqrt_sq_eq_abs]
          exact le_rfl
        · intro x a
          exact sq_nonneg _
        · intro x a
          exact sq_nonneg _
      _ = Real.sqrt (opFamilyDistSq μ A B ψ) *
          Real.sqrt (opFamilyDistSq μ B C ψ) := by
        rfl
  have hdist : opFamilyDistSq μ A C ψ ≤
      (Real.sqrt (opFamilyDistSq μ A B ψ) +
        Real.sqrt (opFamilyDistSq μ B C ψ)) ^ 2 := by
    unfold opFamilyDistSq
    calc
      avgOver μ (fun x =>
          ∑ a : α, ‖applyOperatorToState (A x a - C x a) ψ‖ ^ 2) ≤
          avgOver μ (fun x => ∑ a : α,
            (‖u x a‖ ^ 2 + ‖v x a‖ ^ 2 + 2 * (‖u x a‖ * ‖v x a‖))) := by
        apply avgOver_mono
        intro x
        exact Finset.sum_le_sum fun a _ => hpoint x a
      _ = avgOver μ (fun x => ∑ a : α, ‖u x a‖ ^ 2) +
          avgOver μ (fun x => ∑ a : α, ‖v x a‖ ^ 2) +
          2 * avgOver μ (fun x => ∑ a : α, ‖u x a‖ * ‖v x a‖) := by
        simp_rw [Finset.sum_add_distrib, ← Finset.mul_sum]
        rw [avgOver_add, avgOver_add, avgOver_const_mul]
      _ ≤ avgOver μ (fun x => ∑ a : α, ‖u x a‖ ^ 2) +
          avgOver μ (fun x => ∑ a : α, ‖v x a‖ ^ 2) +
          2 * (Real.sqrt (opFamilyDistSq μ A B ψ) *
            Real.sqrt (opFamilyDistSq μ B C ψ)) := by
        gcongr
      _ = (Real.sqrt (opFamilyDistSq μ A B ψ) +
          Real.sqrt (opFamilyDistSq μ B C ψ)) ^ 2 := by
        change opFamilyDistSq μ A B ψ + opFamilyDistSq μ B C ψ +
          2 * (Real.sqrt (opFamilyDistSq μ A B ψ) *
            Real.sqrt (opFamilyDistSq μ B C ψ)) = _
        have hAB := Real.sq_sqrt (DistanceCalculus.opFamilyDistSq_nonneg μ A B ψ)
        have hBC := Real.sq_sqrt (DistanceCalculus.opFamilyDistSq_nonneg μ B C ψ)
        nlinarith
  calc
    Real.sqrt (opFamilyDistSq μ A C ψ) ≤
        Real.sqrt ((Real.sqrt (opFamilyDistSq μ A B ψ) +
          Real.sqrt (opFamilyDistSq μ B C ψ)) ^ 2) :=
      Real.sqrt_le_sqrt hdist
    _ = |Real.sqrt (opFamilyDistSq μ A B ψ) +
        Real.sqrt (opFamilyDistSq μ B C ψ)| := Real.sqrt_sq_eq_abs _
    _ = Real.sqrt (opFamilyDistSq μ A B ψ) +
        Real.sqrt (opFamilyDistSq μ B C ψ) := by
      rw [abs_of_nonneg (add_nonneg (Real.sqrt_nonneg _) (Real.sqrt_nonneg _))]

/-- Coarsening the outcomes of a projective measurement preserves
projectivity. -/
theorem postprocess_isProjective {α β ι : Type*}
    [Fintype α] [DecidableEq α] [Fintype β] [DecidableEq β]
    [Fintype ι] [DecidableEq ι]
    (M : Measurement α ι) (hM : MIPStarRE.QPBT.Measurement.IsProjective M)
    (f : α → β) : MIPStarRE.QPBT.Measurement.IsProjective (M.postprocess f) := by
  classical
  intro b
  refine { isIdempotentElem := ?_, isSelfAdjoint := ?_ }
  · change (M.postprocess f).effect b * (M.postprocess f).effect b =
      (M.postprocess f).effect b
    simp only [MIPStarRE.Quantum.Measurement.postprocess_effect]
    rw [Finset.sum_mul]
    simp_rw [Finset.mul_sum]
    calc
      (∑ a ∈ Finset.univ.filter (fun a => f a = b),
          ∑ a' ∈ Finset.univ.filter (fun a' => f a' = b),
            M.effect a * M.effect a') =
          ∑ a ∈ Finset.univ.filter (fun a => f a = b),
            ∑ a' ∈ Finset.univ.filter (fun a' => f a' = b),
              if a' = a then M.effect a else 0 := by
        apply Finset.sum_congr rfl
        intro a _
        apply Finset.sum_congr rfl
        intro a' _
        by_cases haa' : a' = a
        · subst a'
          simp [(hM a).isIdempotentElem.eq]
        · rw [if_neg haa']
          exact DistanceCalculus.projective_effect_mul_effect_eq_zero
            M hM (Ne.symm haa')
      _ = ∑ a ∈ Finset.univ.filter (fun a => f a = b), M.effect a := by
        apply Finset.sum_congr rfl
        intro a ha
        simp [ha]
  · change ((M.postprocess f).effect b)ᴴ = (M.postprocess f).effect b
    exact
      (Matrix.nonneg_iff_posSemidef.mp ((M.postprocess f).pos b)).isHermitian.eq

/-- Performing two outcome relabelings has the same effects as their
composition. -/
theorem postprocess_postprocess_effect {α β γ ι : Type*}
    [Fintype α] [DecidableEq α] [Fintype β] [DecidableEq β]
    [Fintype γ] [DecidableEq γ] [Fintype ι] [DecidableEq ι]
    (M : Measurement α ι) (f : α → β) (g : β → γ) (c : γ) :
    ((M.postprocess f).postprocess g).effect c =
      (M.postprocess (fun a => g (f a))).effect c := by
  classical
  simp only [MIPStarRE.Quantum.Measurement.postprocess_effect, Finset.sum_filter]
  calc
    (∑ b : β, if g b = c then
        ∑ a : α, if f a = b then M.effect a else 0 else 0) =
        ∑ b : β, ∑ a : α,
          if g b = c ∧ f a = b then M.effect a else 0 := by
      apply Finset.sum_congr rfl
      intro b _
      by_cases hbc : g b = c <;> simp [hbc]
    _ = ∑ a : α, ∑ b : β,
        if g b = c ∧ f a = b then M.effect a else 0 := by
      rw [Finset.sum_comm]
    _ = ∑ a : α, if g (f a) = c then M.effect a else 0 := by
      apply Finset.sum_congr rfl
      intro a _
      by_cases hac : g (f a) = c
      · rw [Finset.sum_eq_single (f a)]
        · simp [hac]
        · intro b _ hba
          simp [Ne.symm hba]
        · simp
      · apply Eq.trans (Finset.sum_eq_zero (fun b _ => by
          by_cases hab : f a = b
          · subst b
            simp [hac]
          · simp [hab]))
        simp [hac]
    _ = ∑ a : α, if g (f a) = c then M.effect a else 0 := rfl

/-- An injective relabeling does not merge the effect at a relabeled
outcome. -/
theorem postprocess_effect_of_injective {α β ι : Type*}
    [Fintype α] [DecidableEq α] [Fintype β] [DecidableEq β]
    [Fintype ι] [DecidableEq ι]
    (M : Measurement α ι) (f : α → β) (hf : Function.Injective f) (a : α) :
    (M.postprocess f).effect (f a) = M.effect a := by
  simp only [MIPStarRE.Quantum.Measurement.postprocess_effect, Finset.sum_filter]
  rw [Fintype.sum_eq_single a]
  · simp
  · intro z hza
    rw [if_neg]
    exact fun h => hza (hf h)

/-- The squared effects of a POVM sum to at most the identity. -/
theorem measurement_sum_adjoint_mul_le_one {α ι : Type*}
    [Fintype α] [Fintype ι] [DecidableEq ι] (M : Measurement α ι) :
    ∑ a : α, (M.effect a)ᴴ * M.effect a ≤ 1 := by
  calc
    ∑ a : α, (M.effect a)ᴴ * M.effect a =
        ∑ a : α, M.effect a * M.effect a := by
      apply Finset.sum_congr rfl
      intro a _
      rw [DistanceCalculus.measurement_effect_hermitian]
    _ ≤ ∑ a : α, M.effect a := by
      apply Finset.sum_le_sum
      intro a _
      exact MIPStarRE.Quantum.sq_le_self (M.pos a)
        (DistanceCalculus.measurement_effect_le_one M a)
    _ = 1 := M.sum_eq_one

/-- The equal-outcome part of the tensor product of two POVMs is bounded by
the identity. -/
theorem matched_tensor_sum_le_one {α ιA ιB : Type*}
    [Fintype α] [Fintype ιA] [DecidableEq ιA]
    [Fintype ιB] [DecidableEq ιB]
    (A : Measurement α ιA) (B : Measurement α ιB) :
    ∑ a : α, heteroKron (A.effect a) (B.effect a) ≤ 1 := by
  calc
    ∑ a : α, heteroKron (A.effect a) (B.effect a) ≤
        ∑ a : α, ∑ b : α, heteroKron (A.effect a) (B.effect b) := by
      apply Finset.sum_le_sum
      intro a _
      exact Finset.single_le_sum
        (fun b _ => MIPStarRE.Quantum.kronecker_nonneg (A.pos a) (B.pos b))
        (Finset.mem_univ a)
    _ = 1 := by
      ext i j
      simp only [Matrix.sum_apply, heteroKron, Matrix.kronecker,
        Matrix.kroneckerMap_apply]
      simp_rw [← Finset.mul_sum, ← Finset.sum_mul]
      rw [show (∑ a : α, A.effect a i.1 j.1) = (1 : Op ιA) i.1 j.1 by
        simpa only [Matrix.sum_apply] using congrFun (congrFun A.sum_eq_one i.1) j.1]
      rw [show (∑ b : α, B.effect b i.2 j.2) = (1 : Op ιB) i.2 j.2 by
        simpa only [Matrix.sum_apply] using congrFun (congrFun B.sum_eq_one i.2) j.2]
      exact congrFun (congrFun
        (Matrix.one_kronecker_one (m := ιA) (n := ιB) (α := ℂ)) i) j

/-- Multiplying every effect of a POVM on the left by a fixed projective
effect preserves square-summability. -/
theorem projective_mul_measurement_sum_adjoint_mul_le_one
    {α ι : Type*} [Fintype α] [Fintype ι] [DecidableEq ι]
    (P : Op ι) (hP : IsProj P) (M : Measurement α ι) :
    ∑ a : α, (P * M.effect a)ᴴ * (P * M.effect a) ≤ 1 := by
  calc
    ∑ a : α, (P * M.effect a)ᴴ * (P * M.effect a) =
        ∑ a : α, (M.effect a)ᴴ * P * M.effect a := by
      apply Finset.sum_congr rfl
      intro a _
      rw [Matrix.conjTranspose_mul]
      rw [hP.isSelfAdjoint.isHermitian.eq]
      calc
        (M.effect a)ᴴ * P * (P * M.effect a) =
            (M.effect a)ᴴ * ((P * P) * M.effect a) := by
          simp only [mul_assoc]
        _ = (M.effect a)ᴴ * P * M.effect a := by
          rw [hP.isIdempotentElem.eq]
          exact (mul_assoc _ _ _).symm
    _ ≤ ∑ a : α, (M.effect a)ᴴ * M.effect a := by
      apply Finset.sum_le_sum
      intro a _
      simpa [Matrix.star_eq_conjTranspose] using
        star_left_conjugate_le_conjugate hP.le_one (M.effect a)
    _ ≤ 1 := measurement_sum_adjoint_mul_le_one M

/-- Tensoring two projectors gives a projector on the product space. -/
theorem heteroKron_isProj {ιA ιB : Type*}
    [Fintype ιA] [Fintype ιB]
    {P : Op ιA} {Q : Op ιB} (hP : IsProj P) (hQ : IsProj Q) :
    IsProj (heteroKron P Q) := by
  refine { isIdempotentElem := ?_, isSelfAdjoint := ?_ }
  · change heteroKron P Q * heteroKron P Q = heteroKron P Q
    rw [heteroKron_mul, hP.isIdempotentElem.eq, hQ.isIdempotentElem.eq]
  · change (heteroKron P Q)ᴴ = heteroKron P Q
    unfold heteroKron
    simp only [Matrix.kronecker]
    rw [Matrix.conjTranspose_kronecker, hP.isSelfAdjoint.isHermitian.eq,
      hQ.isSelfAdjoint.isHermitian.eq]

/-- The squared effects in one fiber of a pair-valued measurement sum to at
most the identity. -/
theorem measurement_pair_fiber_sum_adjoint_mul_le_one
    {α β ι : Type*} [Fintype α] [Fintype β]
    [Fintype ι] [DecidableEq ι]
    (M : Measurement (α × β) ι) (a : α) :
    ∑ b : β, (M.effect (a, b))ᴴ * M.effect (a, b) ≤ 1 := by
  have hsquare (z : α × β) : (M.effect z)ᴴ * M.effect z ≤ M.effect z := by
    rw [DistanceCalculus.measurement_effect_hermitian]
    exact MIPStarRE.Quantum.sq_le_self (M.pos z)
      (DistanceCalculus.measurement_effect_le_one M z)
  calc
    ∑ b : β, (M.effect (a, b))ᴴ * M.effect (a, b) ≤
        ∑ b : β, M.effect (a, b) := by
      exact Finset.sum_le_sum fun b _ => hsquare (a, b)
    _ ≤ ∑ a' : α, ∑ b : β, M.effect (a', b) := by
      exact Finset.single_le_sum
        (fun a' _ => Finset.sum_nonneg fun b _ => M.pos (a', b))
        (Finset.mem_univ a)
    _ = ∑ z : α × β, M.effect z := (Fintype.sum_prod_type _).symm
    _ = 1 := M.sum_eq_one

/-- A projective joint effect is selected exactly by the matching
postprocessing fiber. -/
theorem postprocess_effect_mul_effect {α β ι : Type*}
    [Fintype α] [DecidableEq α] [Fintype β] [DecidableEq β]
    [Fintype ι] [DecidableEq ι]
    (M : Measurement α ι) (hM : MIPStarRE.QPBT.Measurement.IsProjective M)
    (f : α → β) (b : β) (a : α) :
    (M.postprocess f).effect b * M.effect a =
      if f a = b then M.effect a else 0 := by
  classical
  rw [MIPStarRE.Quantum.Measurement.postprocess_effect, Finset.sum_mul]
  calc
    (∑ z ∈ Finset.univ.filter (fun z => f z = b), M.effect z * M.effect a) =
        ∑ z ∈ Finset.univ.filter (fun z => f z = b),
          if z = a then M.effect a else 0 := by
      apply Finset.sum_congr rfl
      intro z _
      by_cases hza : z = a
      · subst z
        simp [(hM a).isIdempotentElem.eq]
      · rw [if_neg hza]
        exact DistanceCalculus.projective_effect_mul_effect_eq_zero M hM hza
    _ = if f a = b then M.effect a else 0 := by simp

/-- Right-handed form of `postprocess_effect_mul_effect`. -/
theorem effect_mul_postprocess_effect {α β ι : Type*}
    [Fintype α] [DecidableEq α] [Fintype β] [DecidableEq β]
    [Fintype ι] [DecidableEq ι]
    (M : Measurement α ι) (hM : MIPStarRE.QPBT.Measurement.IsProjective M)
    (f : α → β) (b : β) (a : α) :
    M.effect a * (M.postprocess f).effect b =
      if f a = b then M.effect a else 0 := by
  have h := congrArg Matrix.conjTranspose
    (postprocess_effect_mul_effect M hM f b a)
  rw [Matrix.conjTranspose_mul,
    DistanceCalculus.measurement_effect_hermitian M a,
    DistanceCalculus.measurement_effect_hermitian (M.postprocess f) b] at h
  by_cases hab : f a = b
  · simpa [hab, DistanceCalculus.measurement_effect_hermitian M a] using h
  · simpa [hab] using h

/-- Two compatible marginals of a joint projective measurement multiply to
the unique joint effect in their common fiber. -/
theorem postprocess_product_eq_effect {α β γ ι : Type*}
    [Fintype α] [DecidableEq α] [Fintype β] [DecidableEq β]
    [Fintype γ] [DecidableEq γ] [Fintype ι] [DecidableEq ι]
    (M : Measurement α ι) (hM : MIPStarRE.QPBT.Measurement.IsProjective M)
    (f : α → β) (g : α → γ) (a : α)
    (hunique : ∀ z, f z = f a → g z = g a → z = a) :
    (M.postprocess f).effect (f a) * (M.postprocess g).effect (g a) =
      M.effect a := by
  classical
  rw [MIPStarRE.Quantum.Measurement.postprocess_effect M g (g a), Finset.mul_sum]
  calc
    (∑ z ∈ Finset.univ.filter (fun z => g z = g a),
        (M.postprocess f).effect (f a) * M.effect z) =
        ∑ z ∈ Finset.univ.filter (fun z => g z = g a),
          if f z = f a then M.effect z else 0 := by
      apply Finset.sum_congr rfl
      intro z _
      exact postprocess_effect_mul_effect M hM f (f a) z
    _ = M.effect a := by
      rw [Finset.sum_eq_single a]
      · simp
      · intro z hz hza
        rw [if_neg]
        intro hzf
        exact hza (hunique z hzf (Finset.mem_filter.mp hz).2)
      · simp

/-- Left multiplication contracts an operator-family distance when the
multipliers are square-summable on every fiber of the outcome map. -/
theorem opFamilyDistSq_mul_fiber_le {X α Γ ι : Type*}
    [Fintype α] [DecidableEq α] [Fintype Γ] [Fintype ι] [DecidableEq ι]
    (μ : Distribution X) (A B : X → Measurement α ι)
    (eval : Γ → X → α) (S : X → Γ → Op ι)
    (ψ : EuclideanSpace ℂ ι) (δ : ℝ)
    (hS : ∀ x a,
      (1 - ∑ z : Γ, if eval z x = a then (S x z)ᴴ * S x z else 0).PosSemidef)
    (h : opFamilyDistSq μ (fun x a => (A x).effect a)
      (fun x a => (B x).effect a) ψ ≤ δ) :
    opFamilyDistSq μ (fun x z => S x z * (A x).effect (eval z x))
      (fun x z => S x z * (B x).effect (eval z x)) ψ ≤ δ := by
  classical
  apply le_trans ?_ h
  unfold opFamilyDistSq
  apply avgOver_mono
  intro x
  rw [show (∑ z : Γ, ‖applyOperatorToState
      (S x z * (A x).effect (eval z x) - S x z * (B x).effect (eval z x)) ψ‖ ^ 2) =
      ∑ a : α, ∑ z ∈ Finset.univ.filter (fun z => eval z x = a),
        ‖applyOperatorToState
          (S x z * ((A x).effect a - (B x).effect a)) ψ‖ ^ 2 by
    calc
      _ = ∑ a : α, ∑ z ∈ Finset.univ.filter (fun z => eval z x = a),
          ‖applyOperatorToState
            (S x z * (A x).effect (eval z x) -
              S x z * (B x).effect (eval z x)) ψ‖ ^ 2 :=
        (Finset.sum_fiberwise Finset.univ (fun z => eval z x) _).symm
      _ = _ := by
        apply Finset.sum_congr rfl
        intro a _
        apply Finset.sum_congr rfl
        intro z hz
        rw [(Finset.mem_filter.mp hz).2]
        simp only [mul_sub]]
  apply Finset.sum_le_sum
  intro a _
  have hcontract :
      ∑ z : Γ, (if eval z x = a then S x z else 0)ᴴ *
          (if eval z x = a then S x z else 0) ≤ 1 := by
    calc
      ∑ z : Γ, (if eval z x = a then S x z else 0)ᴴ *
          (if eval z x = a then S x z else 0) =
          ∑ z : Γ, if eval z x = a then (S x z)ᴴ * S x z else 0 := by
        apply Finset.sum_congr rfl
        intro z _
        by_cases hza : eval z x = a <;> simp [hza]
      _ ≤ 1 := Matrix.le_iff.mpr (hS x a)
  have hmul := DistanceCalculus.sum_norm_mul_apply_le
    (fun z : Γ => if eval z x = a then S x z else 0)
    ((A x).effect a - (B x).effect a) ψ hcontract
  calc
    (∑ z ∈ Finset.univ.filter (fun z => eval z x = a),
        ‖applyOperatorToState
          (S x z * ((A x).effect a - (B x).effect a)) ψ‖ ^ 2) =
        ∑ z : Γ, if eval z x = a then
          ‖applyOperatorToState
            (S x z * ((A x).effect a - (B x).effect a)) ψ‖ ^ 2 else 0 := by
      rw [Finset.sum_filter]
    _ = ∑ z : Γ, ‖applyOperatorToState
        ((if eval z x = a then S x z else 0) *
          ((A x).effect a - (B x).effect a)) ψ‖ ^ 2 := by
      apply Finset.sum_congr rfl
      intro z _
      by_cases hza : eval z x = a <;> simp [hza, applyOperatorToState]
    _ ≤ ‖applyOperatorToState ((A x).effect a - (B x).effect a) ψ‖ ^ 2 := hmul

private theorem reindexMeasurement_isProjective
    {α I J : Type*} [Fintype α]
    [Fintype I] [DecidableEq I] [Fintype J] [DecidableEq J]
    (e : I ≃ J) (M : Measurement α J)
    (hM : MIPStarRE.QPBT.Measurement.IsProjective M) :

  intro a
  change IsProj (reindexOp e (M.effect a))
  refine { isIdempotentElem := ?_, isSelfAdjoint := ?_ }
  · change (Matrix.reindexAlgEquiv ℂ ℂ e.symm) (M.effect a) *
        (Matrix.reindexAlgEquiv ℂ ℂ e.symm) (M.effect a) =
      (Matrix.reindexAlgEquiv ℂ ℂ e.symm) (M.effect a)
    rw [← map_mul, (hM a).isIdempotentElem.eq]

private theorem measurement_sum_adjoint_mul_le_one
    {α I : Type*} [Fintype α] [Fintype I] [DecidableEq I]
    (M : Measurement α I) :
    ∑ a : α, (M.effect a)ᴴ * M.effect a ≤ 1 := by
  calc

      apply Finset.sum_le_sum
      intro a _
      rw [measurement_effect_hermitian]
      exact MIPStarRE.Quantum.sq_le_self (M.pos a) (measurement_effect_le_one M a)
    _ = 1 := M.sum_eq_one

    {α I J : Type*} [Fintype α]
    [Fintype I] [DecidableEq I] [Fintype J] [DecidableEq J]
    (M : Measurement α J) :
    ∑ a : α, (rightTensor (ι₁ := I) (M.effect a))ᴴ *
        rightTensor (ι₁ := I) (M.effect a) ≤ 1 := by
  calc
    ∑ a : α, (rightTensor (ι₁ := I) (M.effect a))ᴴ *
          rightTensor (ι₁ := I) (M.effect a) =
        rightTensor (ι₁ := I) (∑ a : α, (M.effect a)ᴴ * M.effect a) := by

      apply Finset.sum_congr rfl

      rightTensor_mono (measurement_sum_adjoint_mul_le_one M)

    19	\section{At a glance}
    20	
    21	\begin{itemize}
    22	  \item \textbf{Difficulty.} Medium.  The operator estimate imported by the
    23	  source is plausible, but its stated two-variable polynomial contract is
    24	  contradicted by a two-dimensional example at every fixed positive input
    25	  consistency error.
    26	  \item \textbf{Estimated weight.} Correcting the scalar contract changes one
    27	  shared predicate.  Formalizing the resulting quantitative pasting estimate
    28	  is expected to require roughly 300--600 lines using the existing distance
    29	  calculus.
    30	  \item \textbf{Mathlib/project split.} The obstruction is elementary real
    31	  analysis and finite-dimensional measurement theory.  The repaired proof is
    32	  primarily project-local consistency and Cauchy--Schwarz calculus.
    33	  \item \textbf{Key mathematical inputs.} A positive real power tends to zero
    34	  at zero, while a fixed positive consistency error need not decrease with the
    35	  collision error.
    36	  The discrepancy is tracked in \ghissue{196}.

    39	\section{Key theorem forms}
    40	
    41	The source asks for an error function
    42	$\delta_{\mathrm{pasting}}(\eta,\delta)$ satisfying
    43	\[
    44	  \delta_{\mathrm{pasting}}(\eta,\delta)
    45	    = \operatorname{poly}(\eta,\delta)
    46	\]
    47	and bounding the final consistency defect whenever the three input defects are
    48	at most $\delta$ and the codeword-collision probability is at most $\eta$.
    49	Under the paper's global convention, the displayed polynomial assertion means
    50	that there is a universal $C>0$ such that
    51	\[
    52	  0 \leq \delta_{\mathrm{pasting}}(\eta,\delta)
    53	    \leq C(\eta\delta)^C
    54	  \qquad (\eta,\delta>0).
    55	  \tag{product contract}
    56	\]
    57	The imported proof instead accumulates terms depending separately on the two
    58	errors, including $O(\delta^{1/2})$, $O((\delta+\eta)^{1/2})$, and $\eta$.
    59	A compatible corrected theorem form would use, for example, an upper bound by
    60	$A(\eta^r+\delta^s)$ for universal $A\geq1$ and $r,s>0$.
    61	
    62	\section{The source assertion}
    63	
    64	Lemma~\texttt{lem:pasting} of \cite[lines~504--525]{Ji2020MIPStar} imports
    65	Fact~4.35 from the NEEXP paper.  Its error is declared to be
    66	$\operatorname{poly}(\eta,\delta)$.  The asymptotic convention in
    67	\cite[lines~19--29]{Ji2020MIPStar} requires every variable to occur in the
    68	product on the right side of the product contract.  The proof of the imported
    69	fact, however, bounds the two sources of error independently; see
    70	\cite[lines~1030--1209]{Natarajan2018NEEXP}.%
    71	\footnote{The mirrored passages are
    72	\path{references/qpbt-paper/04_preliminaries.tex}, lines~19--29;
    73	\path{references/qpbt-paper/06_nonlocal_games_and_mipstar.tex}, lines~504--525;
    74	and \path{references/neexp-paper/05_quantum_preliminaries.tex},
    75	lines~1030--1209.}

    77	\section{A two-dimensional counterexample}
    78	
    79	Fix $0<\rho<1$.  Let every question set, both codeword sets, and the second
    80	answer set be a singleton, and let the first answer set be $\{0,1\}$.  Use the
    81	point-mass question distribution and local Hilbert spaces $\C^2$.  In the
    82	standard basis, take the normalized bipartite state
    83	\[
    84	  \ket{\psi_\rho}
    85	    = \sqrt{1-\rho}\ket{0,0}+\sqrt{\rho}\ket{1,1}.
    86	\]
    87	Let both codeword measurements have their sole effect equal to the identity,
    88	and evaluate the sole first codeword to $0$.  Let the joint answer measurement
    89	be the standard-basis projective measurement: its effects at $(0,*)$ and
    90	$(1,*)$ are respectively $\ket{0}\!\bra{0}$ and $\ket{1}\!\bra{1}$.
    91	
    92	The second codeword set is a singleton, so its pairwise-collision hypothesis is
    93	vacuous for every $\eta\geq0$.  The second marginal is exactly consistent, and
    94	the perfectly correlated state makes the joint answer measurement exactly
    95	self-consistent.  The first marginal differs from the constantly-zero
    96	codeword answer precisely on the $\ket{1,1}$ component, so its consistency
    97	defect is $\rho$.  Consequently all hypotheses of the pasting lemma hold with
    98	$\delta=\rho$.
    99	
   100	The pasted measurement also has a single codeword outcome and its effect is the
   101	identity.  After evaluation it is deterministic at $(0,*)$, whereas the joint
   102	answer measurement returns $(1,*)$ with probability $\rho$.  Their final
   103	consistency defect is therefore $\rho$.  Thus the asserted conclusion would
   104	require
   105	\[
   106	  \rho \leq \delta_{\mathrm{pasting}}(\eta,\rho)
   107	  \qquad\text{for every }\eta>0.
   108	\]
   109	The product contract gives the opposite asymptotic bound
   110	$\delta_{\mathrm{pasting}}(\eta,\rho)\leq C(\eta\rho)^C$.  Since $C>0$, the
   111	right side tends to zero with $\eta$, which is a contradiction.  As $\rho$ can
   112	be arbitrarily small, this failure is not confined to the large-error boundary.
   113	
   114	\section{Comparison with the blueprint and formalization}
   115	
   116	The blueprint reproduces the source theorem and its unrestricted nonnegative
   117	error parameters.  The formal predicate implements the product contract
   118	literally, and the paper-facing pasting declaration retains the same theorem
   119	form.%
   120	\footnote{The polynomial predicate is defined in
   121	\doclink{MIPStarRE/QPBT/Games/ErrorFunctions.lean}; the paper-facing theorem is
   122	\leanid{exists\_pasting\_error} in
   123	\doclink{MIPStarRE/QPBT/Games/Sandwich.lean}.}
   124	The declaration must remain without a proof-complete blueprint marker until the
   125	scalar contract is corrected or the source theorem is restricted.  The
   126	operator-valued pasting construction itself is not refuted by this example.
   127	
   128	\section{Conclusion}
   129	
   130	The literal product-form interpretation of
   131	$\operatorname{poly}(\eta,\delta)$ makes the stated pasting lemma false.  This
   132	is a theorem-level scalar discrepancy, not a missing formal-library lemma.  The
   133	natural repair is to adopt a multivariate polynomial-smallness convention that
   134	allows separate positive powers of the input errors, matching the terms in the
   135	imported proof.  Adding an unadvertised coupling hypothesis between $\eta$ and
   136	$\delta$ would also avoid the counterexample, but would strengthen the source
   137	theorem and is therefore not the preferred repair.

   469	\begin{lemma}[Sandwiched simultaneous measurement; modified from Fact 4.34 in \cite{Natarajan2018NEEXP}]\label{lem:ld-sandwich}
   470		\lean{MIPStarRE.QPBT.sandwichProduct}

   474		Let $k \ge 0$ be an integer and let $\eps > 0$. Let $\mathcal X$ be a finite set and $\mu$ a distribution over $\mathcal X$, and let $\mathcal Y$ be a finite nonempty set; all statements below that sample $y \in \mathcal Y$ refer to the uniform distribution on $\mathcal Y$. For each $1 \le i \le k$ let $\mathcal R_i$ be a finite set, let $\mathcal G_i$ be a finite set of functions $g_i \colon \mathcal Y \to \mathcal R_i$, and for each $x \in \mathcal X$ let $\{G^{i,\,x}_g\}_{g \in \mathcal G_i}$ be a projective measurement. Suppose that for all $i \in \{1,\dots,k\}$ the set $\mathcal G_i$ satisfies the following property: for any two $g_i \ne g_i' \in \mathcal G_i$, the probability that $g_i(y) = g_i'(y)$ over a uniformly random $y \in \mathcal Y$ is at most $\eps$.
   475		Index the factors by $0,\ldots,k-1$; factor $r$ corresponds to the paper's
   476		factor $r+1$.
   477	
   478		Let $\bigl\{ A^x_{g_1,\,g_2,\,\dots,\,g_k} \bigr\}$ be a projective measurement with outcomes $(g_1,\dots,g_k) \in \mathcal G_1 \times \cdots \times \mathcal G_k$. Here $\operatorname{eval}_y$ denotes the evaluation map $g \mapsto g(y)$, so that $A^x_{[\operatorname{eval}_y(\cdot)_i = a_i]}$ post-processes the outcome tuple by evaluating its $i$-th component at $y$; since the outcome sets $\mathcal G_1 \times \cdots \times \mathcal G_k$ and $\mathcal G_i$ and the targets $\mathcal R_i$ are finite, these are post-processings in the sense of Definition~\ref{def:bracket}. For each $1 \le i \le k$, suppose that on average over $x \sim \mu$ and $y \in \mathcal Y$ sampled uniformly at random,
   479		\begin{equation}\label{eq:ld-sandwich-1}
   480			A^x_{[\operatorname{eval}_y(\cdot)_i = a_i]} \ot \Id_B \simeq_{\delta} \Id_A \ot G^{i,\,x}_{[\operatorname{eval}_y(\cdot) = a_i]}\,.
   481		\end{equation}
   482		% The source (references/qpbt-paper/06_nonlocal_games_and_mipstar.tex:465-495) prints the
   483		% transposed pairing G^{k,x}_{g_1} ... G^{1,x}_{g_k} ... G^{k,x}_{g_1}, which is undefined
   484		% when the outcome sets differ; the pairing below is the one of Fact 4.34 in the NEEXP
   485		% source. The empty product for k = 0 is also made explicit here. See
   486		% rem:ld-sandwich-indexing.
   487		Define the POVM family $\{C^x_{g_1,\,g_2,\,\dots,\,g_k}\}$, for $x \in \mathcal X$, by
   488		\[
   489			C^x_{g_1,\,g_2,\,\dots,\,g_k} = G^{k,\,x}_{g_k} \cdots G^{2,\,x}_{g_2}\; G^{1,\,x}_{g_1}\; G^{2,\,x}_{g_2} \cdots G^{k,\,x}_{g_k}\,;
   490		\]
   491		for $k = 0$ the empty product is understood as the identity, so that $C^x$ is the measurement whose single outcome, the empty tuple, carries the operator $\Id$. Then on average over $x \sim \mu$ and $y \in \mathcal Y$ sampled uniformly at random,
   492		\begin{equation}\label{eq:ld-sandwich-2}
   493			A^x_{[\operatorname{eval}_y(\cdot) = (a_1,\,a_2,\,\dots,\,a_k)]} \ot \Id_B \simeq_{k(\delta+\eps)^{1/2}} \Id_A \ot C^x_{[\operatorname{eval}_y(\cdot) = (a_1,\,a_2,\,\dots,\,a_k)]}\,.
   494		\end{equation}

   497		\leanok
   498		The source proof is a citation: the argument is identical to the proof of Fact 4.34 in \cite{Natarajan2018NEEXP}, with the only modification being the insertion of the dependence on the question $x$ for all measurements considered. In outline, the consistency hypotheses \eqref{eq:ld-sandwich-1} allow one to insert the projective factors $G^{i,\,x}$ next to $A^x$ one index at a time, and the $\eps$-bound on the pairwise agreement of distinct functions in $\mathcal G_i$ controls the events on which two different outcomes collide at the sampled point $y$. Each of the $k$ insertions costs $(\delta+\eps)^{1/2}$ by the Cauchy--Schwarz inequality, producing the sandwich $C^x$ with total error $k(\delta+\eps)^{1/2}$.
