+\documentclass[11pt]{article}
+
+\usepackage{amsmath,amssymb}
+\usepackage{xurl}
+\usepackage[hidelinks]{hyperref}
+\setlength{\emergencystretch}{2em}
+
+\input{command}
+\renewcommand{\ghissue}[1]{%
+  \href{https://github.com/Dengnifer/MIPStarRE-A/issues/#1}{GitHub issue \##1}}
+
+\title{The Product-Form Error in the Two-Measurement Pasting Lemma}
+\author{}
+\date{2026-09-05}
+
+\begin{document}
+\maketitle
+
+\section{At a glance}
+
+\begin{itemize}
+  \item \textbf{Difficulty.} Medium.  The operator estimate imported by the
+  source is plausible, but its stated two-variable polynomial contract is
+  contradicted by a two-dimensional example at every fixed positive input
+  consistency error.
+  \item \textbf{Estimated weight.} Correcting the scalar contract changes one
+  shared predicate.  Formalizing the resulting quantitative pasting estimate
+  is expected to require roughly 300--600 lines using the existing distance
+  calculus.
+  \item \textbf{Mathlib/project split.} The obstruction is elementary real
+  analysis and finite-dimensional measurement theory.  The repaired proof is
+  primarily project-local consistency and Cauchy--Schwarz calculus.
+  \item \textbf{Key mathematical inputs.} A positive real power tends to zero
+  at zero, while a fixed positive consistency error need not decrease with the
+  collision error.
+  The discrepancy is tracked in \ghissue{196}.
+\end{itemize}
+
+\section{Key theorem forms}
+
+The source asks for an error function
+$\delta_{\mathrm{pasting}}(\eta,\delta)$ satisfying
+\[
+  \delta_{\mathrm{pasting}}(\eta,\delta)
+    = \operatorname{poly}(\eta,\delta)
+\]
+and bounding the final consistency defect whenever the three input defects are
+at most $\delta$ and the codeword-collision probability is at most $\eta$.
+Under the paper's global convention, the displayed polynomial assertion means
+that there is a universal $C>0$ such that
+\[
+  0 \leq \delta_{\mathrm{pasting}}(\eta,\delta)
+    \leq C(\eta\delta)^C
+  \qquad (\eta,\delta>0).
+  \tag{product contract}
+\]
+The imported proof instead accumulates terms depending separately on the two
+errors, including $O(\delta^{1/2})$, $O((\delta+\eta)^{1/2})$, and $\eta$.
+A compatible corrected theorem form would use, for example, an upper bound by
+$A(\eta^r+\delta^s)$ for universal $A\geq1$ and $r,s>0$.
+
+\section{The source assertion}
+
+Lemma~\texttt{lem:pasting} of \cite[lines~504--525]{Ji2020MIPStar} imports
+Fact~4.35 from the NEEXP paper.  Its error is declared to be
+$\operatorname{poly}(\eta,\delta)$.  The asymptotic convention in
+\cite[lines~19--29]{Ji2020MIPStar} requires every variable to occur in the
+product on the right side of the product contract.  The proof of the imported
+fact, however, bounds the two sources of error independently; see
+\cite[lines~1030--1209]{Natarajan2018NEEXP}.%
+\footnote{The mirrored passages are
+\path{references/qpbt-paper/04_preliminaries.tex}, lines~19--29;
+\path{references/qpbt-paper/06_nonlocal_games_and_mipstar.tex}, lines~504--525;
+and \path{references/neexp-paper/05_quantum_preliminaries.tex},
+lines~1030--1209.}
+
+\section{A two-dimensional counterexample}
+
+Fix $0<\rho<1$.  Let every question set, both codeword sets, and the second
+answer set be a singleton, and let the first answer set be $\{0,1\}$.  Use the
+point-mass question distribution and local Hilbert spaces $\C^2$.  In the
+standard basis, take the normalized bipartite state
+\[
+  \ket{\psi_\rho}
+    = \sqrt{1-\rho}\ket{0,0}+\sqrt{\rho}\ket{1,1}.
+\]
+Let both codeword measurements have their sole effect equal to the identity,
+and evaluate the sole first codeword to $0$.  Let the joint answer measurement
+be the standard-basis projective measurement: its effects at $(0,*)$ and
+$(1,*)$ are respectively $\ket{0}\!\bra{0}$ and $\ket{1}\!\bra{1}$.
+
+The second codeword set is a singleton, so its pairwise-collision hypothesis is
+vacuous for every $\eta\geq0$.  The second marginal is exactly consistent, and
+the perfectly correlated state makes the joint answer measurement exactly
+self-consistent.  The first marginal differs from the constantly-zero
+codeword answer precisely on the $\ket{1,1}$ component, so its consistency
+defect is $\rho$.  Consequently all hypotheses of the pasting lemma hold with
+$\delta=\rho$.
+
+The pasted measurement also has a single codeword outcome and its effect is the
+identity.  After evaluation it is deterministic at $(0,*)$, whereas the joint
+answer measurement returns $(1,*)$ with probability $\rho$.  Their final
+consistency defect is therefore $\rho$.  Thus the asserted conclusion would
+require
+\[
+  \rho \leq \delta_{\mathrm{pasting}}(\eta,\rho)
+  \qquad\text{for every }\eta>0.
+\]
+The product contract gives the opposite asymptotic bound
+$\delta_{\mathrm{pasting}}(\eta,\rho)\leq C(\eta\rho)^C$.  Since $C>0$, the
+right side tends to zero with $\eta$, which is a contradiction.  As $\rho$ can
+be arbitrarily small, this failure is not confined to the large-error boundary.
+
+\section{Comparison with the blueprint and formalization}
+
+The blueprint reproduces the source theorem and its unrestricted nonnegative
+error parameters.  The formal predicate implements the product contract
+literally, and the paper-facing pasting declaration retains the same theorem
+form.%
+\footnote{The polynomial predicate is defined in
+\doclink{MIPStarRE/QPBT/Games/ErrorFunctions.lean}; the paper-facing theorem is
+\leanid{exists\_pasting\_error} in
+\doclink{MIPStarRE/QPBT/Games/Sandwich.lean}.}
+The declaration must remain without a proof-complete blueprint marker until the
+scalar contract is corrected or the source theorem is restricted.  The
+operator-valued pasting construction itself is not refuted by this example.
+
+\section{Conclusion}
+
+The literal product-form interpretation of
+$\operatorname{poly}(\eta,\delta)$ makes the stated pasting lemma false.  This
+is a theorem-level scalar discrepancy, not a missing formal-library lemma.  The
+natural repair is to adopt a multivariate polynomial-smallness convention that
+allows separate positive powers of the input errors, matching the terms in the
+imported proof.  Adding an unadvertised coupling hypothesis between $\eta$ and
+$\delta$ would also avoid the counterexample, but would strengthen the source
+theorem and is therefore not the preferred repair.
+
+\bibliographystyle{alpha}
+\bibliography{references}
+
+\end{document}

/-!
# The directly indexed low-degree game

The low-degree game used by the Pauli-basis combining argument is needed in
dimension `2 * m + 2`.  The existing conditionally linear game represents a
coordinate index by an equally sized fiber in the scalar field and therefore
requires the dimension to divide the field size.  This file gives the separate
directly indexed variant which samples that index directly.

The geometric line carrier records the sampled coordinate, and line evaluation
uses an `Option` outcome rather than assigning a value when a point does not
determine one.  The game retains the point, axis-line, and diagonal-line answer
formats and the nine ordered type branches of the original low-degree game.

The `Transport` modules relate the direct game to the seed-indexed game and to
the mature low individual degree test interface: `Transport.Correspondence`
identifies coordinates, answers, and the question law of the two QPBT
presentations; `Transport.SeedFiber` dilates a seed-indexed strategy to a
direct strategy by a correlated residue register, and `Transport.SeedFiberValue`
shows that the dilation preserves the value exactly; `Transport.Questions`
reads mature lines as canonical direct questions and rebases direct answers;
`Transport.Strategy` reads one coordinate of a projective direct strategy as a
mature `ProjStrat`, with exact Born-weight formulas for both adapters; and
`Transport.BranchComparison`, `Transport.DiagonalRecursion`, and
`Transport.PassConversion` convert a value bound of the direct game into the
pass hypothesis of the mature low individual degree theorem for every
coordinate strategy.  `GameValue` supplies the rejection calculus relating the
direct value to the mature branch weights.  `Transport.Error` carries the
scalar half of the transport: the auxiliary sampling parameter with which
the mature theorem is applied, bounds on the three terms of its error
function, and the absorption of the resulting simultaneous-measurement
estimate into the error function of `lem:ld-soundness`.
`Transport.Consistency` identifies polynomial outcomes and transports the
three mature consistency conclusions to the direct game.

## References

The underlying game is `def:ld-game` in
`blueprint/src/chapter/ch13_qpbt_test.tex:17-105`, with source origin
`references/qpbt-paper/08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:31-391`.
The need for the directly indexed repair in Chapter 15 is explained around
`rem:qld-4-7-divisibility` in
`blueprint/src/chapter/ch15_qpbt_combining.tex:1257-1293` and in
`docs/paper-gaps/qpbt_ld-dimension-divisibility.tex`.
-/

   259	    (params : Parameters)

   160	Thus, it will be convenient to introduce the following notation.
   161	Let $(\psi, A, B, L)$ be a symmetric strategy for the $(m+1, q, d)$-low individual degree test,
   162	Then for each $u \in \F_q^m$ we will write $B^u_f$ as shorthand for $B^{\ell}_f$,
   163	where $\ell = \{(u, x) \mid x \in \F_q\}$.
   164	For a function $f:\ell \rightarrow \F_q$,
   165	we will also sometimes write $f(x)$ as shorthand for $f(u,x)$.
   166	\end{notation}
   167	
   168	\begin{definition}
   169	Consider the $(m,q,d)$-low individual degree test.
   170	For $j \in \{1, \ldots, m\}$,
   171	we refer to the \emph{$j$-restricted diagonal lines test}
   172	as the diagonal lines test conditioned on $\bi = j$.
   173	For example, in the $m$-restricted diagonal lines test,
   174	the line $\bell$ is simply a uniformly random line in $\F_q^m$.
   175	\end{definition}
   176	
   177	Now we state our main theorem using notation which will be introduced in \Cref{sec:prelims} below.
   178	This the formal version of \Cref{thm:main-informal}.
   179	
   180	\begin{theorem}[Main theorem; quantum soundness of the low individual degree test]\label{thm:main-formal}
   181	  Consider a projective strategy $(\psi, A^{\mathrm{A}},B^{\mathrm{A}},L^{\mathrm{A}},A^{\mathrm{B}},B^{\mathrm{B}},L^{\mathrm{B}})$ 
   182	   which passes the  $(m,q,d)$-low individual degree test with probability at least $1-\eps$.
   183	  Let $k \geq md$ be an integer.
   184	  Let
   185	  \begin{equation*}
   186	  \nu = 100000 k^2m^4 \cdot \Big(\eps^{1/40000} + (d/q)^{1/40000} + e^{-k/(2560000m^2)}\Big).
   187	  \end{equation*}
   188	Then there exists projective measurements $G^{\mathrm{A}}, G^{\mathrm{B}} \in \polymeas{m}{q}{d}$ with the following properties:
   189	\begin{enumerate}
   190	  \item (Consistency with~$A$):  On average over $\bu \sim \F_q^{m}$,
   191		  \begin{align*}
   192		  A^{\mathrm{A},u}_a \otimes I
   193		  	&\simeq_{\nu} I \otimes G^{\mathrm{B}}_{[g(u)=a]},\\
   194		I \otimes A^{\mathrm{B},u}_a
   195		  	&\simeq_{\nu}  G^{\mathrm{A}}_{[g(u)=a]} \ot I.
   196		  \end{align*}
   197	\item (Self-consistency):
   198		\begin{equation*}
   199		G^{\mathrm{A}}_g \ot I \simeq_{\nu} I \ot G^{\mathrm{B}}_g.
   200		\end{equation*}
   201	\end{enumerate}
   202	\end{theorem}
   203	
   204	We note that there is a tradeoff in \Cref{thm:main-formal} specified by the parameter~$k$.
   205	As~$k$ increases, $\nu$'s prefactor $k^2$ increases.
   206	On the other hand, as $k$ increases, the term $e^{- k/(2560000m^2)}$ which also occurs in $\nu$ \emph{decreases}.
   207	Thus, when applying this theorem, one must select~$k$ to balance these competing demands.
   208	Typically, choosing $k = \poly(m)$ should be more than sufficient for applications.
   209	We believe that this parameter~$k$ is an artifact of our proof,
   210	and we hope that it will be removed in the future.
   211

   332	noncomputable def averageDiagonalBlock
   333	    {iota block : Type*} [Fintype iota] [Fintype block]
   334	    (A : Op (iota × block)) : Op iota := by
   335	  classical
   336	  exact (Fintype.card block : ℝ)⁻¹ •
   337	    ∑ r, A.submatrix (fun i => (i, r)) (fun i => (i, r))

   339	/-- Compress a POVM through the normalized diagonal-block average.  The
   340	nonemptiness assumption says precisely that the normalized finite average is
   341	defined over at least one ancillary basis element. -/
   342	noncomputable def correlatedAncillaCompressMeasurement
   343	    {alpha iota block : Type*}
   344	    [Fintype alpha] [Fintype iota] [DecidableEq iota]
   345	    [Fintype block] [DecidableEq block] [Nonempty block]
   346	    (M : MIPStarRE.Quantum.Measurement alpha (iota × block)) :
   347	    MIPStarRE.Quantum.Measurement alpha iota :=
   348	  MIPStarRE.Quantum.Measurement.ofSumEqOne
   349	    (fun a => averageDiagonalBlock (M.effect a))
   350	    (fun a => by
   351	      unfold averageDiagonalBlock
   352	      apply smul_nonneg
   353	      · positivity
   354	      · exact Finset.sum_nonneg fun r _ =>
   355	          Matrix.nonneg_iff_posSemidef.mpr
   356	            ((Matrix.nonneg_iff_posSemidef.mp (M.pos a)).submatrix
   357	              (fun i => (i, r))))
   358	    (by
   359	      classical
   360	      ext i j
   361	      simp only [averageDiagonalBlock, Matrix.sum_apply, Matrix.smul_apply,
   362	        Matrix.submatrix_apply]
   363	      calc
   364	        ∑ a, (Fintype.card block : ℝ)⁻¹ •
   365	              ∑ r, M.effect a (i, r) (j, r) =
   366	            (Fintype.card block : ℝ)⁻¹ •
   367	              ∑ a, ∑ r, M.effect a (i, r) (j, r) := by
   368	                rw [Finset.smul_sum]
   369	        _ = (Fintype.card block : ℝ)⁻¹ •
   370	              ∑ r, ∑ a, M.effect a (i, r) (j, r) := by
   371	                rw [Finset.sum_comm]
   372	        _ = (Fintype.card block : ℝ)⁻¹ •
   373	              ∑ r, (1 : Op (iota × block)) (i, r) (j, r) := by
   374	                congr 1
   375	                apply Finset.sum_congr rfl
   376	                intro r _
   377	                simpa only [Matrix.sum_apply] using
   378	                  congrFun (congrFun M.sum_eq_one (i, r)) (j, r)

    24	/-- Recursive form of the palindromic operator product, extending a tuple by
    25	placing its final operator on both sides of the preceding product. -/
    26	private noncomputable def sandwichProductCore {ι : Type*}
    27	    [Fintype ι] [DecidableEq ι] :
    28	    (k : ℕ) → (Γ : Fin k → Type*) →
    29	      ((i : Fin k) → Γ i → Op ι) → ((i : Fin k) → Γ i) → Op ι
    30	  | 0, _, _, _ => 1
    31	  | 1, _, G, g => G 0 (g 0)
    32	  | k + 2, Γ, G, g =>
    33	      G (Fin.last (k + 1)) (g (Fin.last (k + 1))) *
    34	        sandwichProductCore (k + 1) (fun i => Γ i.castSucc)
    35	          (fun i a => G i.castSucc a) (fun i => g i.castSucc) *
    36	        G (Fin.last (k + 1)) (g (Fin.last (k + 1)))

   145	                  sandwichProductCore (k + 2) Γ
   146	                    (fun i a => (G i x).effect a) g) =
   147	                  ∑ p : Γ (Fin.last (k + 1)) ×
   148	                      ((i : Fin (k + 1)) → Γ i.castSucc),
   149	                    sandwichProductCore (k + 2) Γ

   159	                rw [Fintype.sum_prod_type]

   161	                intro a _
   162	                apply Finset.sum_congr rfl

   164	                simp [sandwichProductCore]

   166	                    (G (Fin.last (k + 1)) x).effect a *

        simp [Matrix.single, hio, hjo, and_comm]).isSelfAdjoint

/-- The `Option` basis projectors sum to the identity. -/
lemma optionBasisProj_sum_eq_one {α : Type*} [Fintype α] [DecidableEq α] :
    ∑ oa : Option α, (Matrix.single oa oa (1 : ℂ) : MIPStarRE.Quantum.Op (Option α)) = 1 := by
  ext i j
  by_cases hij : i = j
  · subst hij
    cases i with
    | none =>
        rw [Fintype.sum_option]
        simp [Matrix.sum_apply]
    | some a =>
        rw [Fintype.sum_option]
        simp [Matrix.sum_apply, Matrix.single_apply]
  · rw [Fintype.sum_option]
    cases i with
    | none =>
        cases j with
        | none => cases hij rfl
        | some b =>
            simp [Matrix.sum_apply]
    | some a =>
        cases j with
        | none =>
            simp [Matrix.sum_apply]
        | some b =>
            have hab : a ≠ b := fun h => hij (congrArg some h)
            simp [Matrix.sum_apply, Matrix.single_apply, hab]

/-- Kronecker products of projectors are projective. -/
lemma isProj_kronecker {d₁ d₂ : Type*}
    [Fintype d₁] [Fintype d₂]
    {A : MIPStarRE.Quantum.Op d₁} {B : MIPStarRE.Quantum.Op d₂}
    (hA : MIPStarRE.Quantum.IsProj A) (hB : MIPStarRE.Quantum.IsProj B) :
    MIPStarRE.Quantum.IsProj (Matrix.kronecker A B) := by
  refine { isIdempotentElem := ?_, isSelfAdjoint := ?_ }
  · calc
      Matrix.kronecker A B * Matrix.kronecker A B
          = Matrix.kronecker (A * A) (B * B) := by
              simpa using (Matrix.mul_kronecker_mul A A B B).symm
      _ = Matrix.kronecker A B := by rw [hA.isIdempotentElem.eq, hB.isIdempotentElem.eq]
  · exact (Matrix.IsHermitian.ext fun i j => by
      cases i with
      | mk i₁ i₂ =>
          cases j with
          | mk j₁ j₂ =>
              simp [Matrix.kronecker, hA.isSelfAdjoint.isHermitian.apply,
                hB.isSelfAdjoint.isHermitian.apply]).isSelfAdjoint

/-- Unitary conjugation preserves projectivity. -/
lemma isProj_unitary_conj {n : Type*} [Fintype n] [DecidableEq n]
    (U : Matrix.unitaryGroup n ℂ) {P : MIPStarRE.Quantum.Op n}
    (hP : MIPStarRE.Quantum.IsProj P) :
    MIPStarRE.Quantum.IsProj
      (((U : MIPStarRE.Quantum.Op n)ᴴ) * P * (U : MIPStarRE.Quantum.Op n)) := by
  refine { isIdempotentElem := ?_, isSelfAdjoint := ?_ }
  · calc

/-- Postprocessing is functorial: postprocessing by `f` and then by `g`
agrees with a single postprocessing by the composite `g ∘ f`. -/
@[simp] theorem postprocess_comp {α β γ : Type*} {ι : Type*}
    [Fintype α] [Fintype β] [Fintype γ] [Fintype ι] [DecidableEq ι]
    (A : SubMeas α ι) (f : α → β) (g : β → γ) :
    postprocess (postprocess A f) g = postprocess A (fun a => g (f a)) := by
  classical
  refine SubMeas.ext ?_ rfl
  intro c
  calc
    (postprocess (postprocess A f) g).outcome c
        = ∑ b : β,
            if g b = c then
              ∑ a : α, if f a = b then A.outcome a else 0
            else 0 := by

    (params : Parameters) [FieldModel params.q]
    (H : SubMeas (Polynomial params.next) ι) (u : Point params.next) :
    postprocess

      (fun f => f (pointHeight params u)) =
    evaluateAt params.next u H := by
  let verticalLine : AxisParallelLine params.next :=

  rw [show hRestrictionToVerticalLine params H (truncatePoint params u) =
      postprocess H (fun h => Polynomial.restrictToAxisParallelLine params.next h verticalLine) by
      rfl]

  have happend : appendPoint params (truncatePoint params u) (pointHeight params u) = u := by
    exact (pointNextEquiv params).left_inv u

      AxisParallelLine.pointAt verticalLine (pointHeight params u)

            simpa [verticalLine] using

                (truncatePoint params u) (pointHeight params u)

   390	    zeroes out the first $i-1$ coordinates of $v$.}
   391	  \label{fig:ld-decider}
   392	\end{figure}
   393	
   394	We define a special class of measurements that are relevant to the soundness
   395	properties of the low-degree test.
   396	
   397	\begin{definition}[Low-degree polynomial measurements]
   398	  \label{def:ld-meas}
   399	  Define $\polymeas{m}{d}{q}$ to be the set of POVM measurements whose outcomes
   400	  correspond to (individual) degree-$d$ polynomials of $m$ variables over
   401	  $\F_q$.
   402	  More generally, for an integer $\ldc$ and tuples $m=(m_1, m_2, \ldots,
   403	  m_\ldc)$, $d=(d_1, d_2, \ldots, d_\ldc)$ and $q=(q_1, q_2, \ldots, q_\ldc)$,
   404	  we let $\simulpolymeas{m}{d}{q}{\ldc}$ be the set of measurements $G =
   405	  \{G_{g_1,\, g_2,\, \ldots\,,\, g_\ldc}\}$ such that for $i\in\{1, 2, \ldots,
   406	  \ldc\}$, $g_i$ is a polynomial $g_i:\F_{q_i}^{m_i} \rightarrow
   407	  \F_{q_i}$ with individual degree $d_i$ (see \Cref{sec:ld-encoding} for a definition of individual degree). 
   408	\end{definition}
   409	
   410	Quantum soundness of a version of the classical low-degree test for polynomials of low \emph{total} degree was claimed
   411	in~\cite{natarajan2018low}, building on an analysis of a three-prover version of the test in~\cite{vidick2016three}. Unfortunately there is a gap in the soundness analysis of this test. For our construction we use the low individual degree test, whose quantum soundness is shown in~\cite{ML20} and generalized in~\cite{ji2021quantum}. We state the result in the form that is most directly useful for us, and show how the stated result follows from~\cite{ji2021quantum}.
   412	
   413	\begin{theorem}[Quantum soundness of the simultaneous classical low-degree test]
   414	  \label{lem:ld-soundness}
   415	  There exists a function $\delta_{\ld}(\eps, q, m, d, \ldc) = a (dm \ldc)^a (\eps^b + q^{-b} + 2^{-bmd})$ for universal constants $a\geq 1$ and $0<b\leq 1$ 
   416	such that the following
   417	  holds.
   418	  For all $\eps > 0$ and parameter tuple $\ldparams = (q, m, d, \ldc)$, for all
   419	  projective strategies $(\psi,A,B)$ that succeed with probability at least
   420	  $1-\eps$ in the game $\game^\ld_\ldparams$, there exists measurements
   421	  \[G^w \in \simulpolymeas{m}{d}{q}{\ldc}\] on $\mH_w$, for
   422	  $w\in\{\alice,\bob\}$, such that
   423	  \begin{equation*}
   424	    \begin{split}
   425	      A^{\Point,\, u}_{a_1,\, a_2,\, \ldots\,,\, a_\ldc}
   426	      & \abc[\delta_{\ld}]
   427	      G^\bob_{[(g_1(u),g_2(u),\ldots,g_\ldc(u)) = (a_1,\, a_2,\, \ldots \,,\, a_\ldc)]}\;,\\
   428	      G^\alice_{[(g_1(u),g_2(u),\ldots,g_\ldc(u)) = (a_1,\, a_2,\, \ldots \,,\, a_\ldc)]}
   429	      & \abc[\delta_{\ld}]
   430				 B^{\Point,\, u}_{a_1,\, a_2,\, \ldots\,,\, a_\ldc}\;,\\
   431	      G^\alice_{g_1,\, g_2,\, \ldots \,,\, g_\ldc}
   432	      & \abc[\delta_{\ld}]
   433	      G^\bob_{g_1,\, g_2,\, \ldots \,,\, g_\ldc}\;,
   434	    \end{split}
   435	  \end{equation*}
   436	  where $\delta_{\ld} = \delta_{\ld}(\eps, q, m, d, \ldc)$, 
   437	  and all three statements are with respect to the state $\ket{\psi}$.
   438	In addition, the first two approximations hold under the uniform distribution over $u\in \F_q^m$,
   439		whereas there is no question distribution associated with the third approximation.
   440	\end{theorem}
   441	
   442	\begin{proof}
   443	Let $\ldparams = (q, m, d, \ldc)$
   444	where $m, d, \ldc \in \N$ are integers, $q \in \N$ is an admissible field size,
   445	and $m$ divides $q$. Let $\Sigma=\F_q$. Let $\code \subseteq \Sigma^q$ be the Reed-Solomon code with degree $d$. Explicitly, $\code$ is the set of all $(p(x_1),\ldots,p(x_n))$ where $p:\F_q\to\F_q$ is a univariate polynomial of degree at most $d$ and $x_1,\ldots,x_n$ are an enumeration of $\F_q$. Then in the (standard) notation from~\cite{ji2021quantum} $\code$ is a linear $[q,d+1,n-d+1]_\Sigma$ code.
   446	
   447	Observe that the two-prover tensor code test, for the code $\code^{\otimes m}$, as described in~\cite[Figure 1 and Figure 2]{ji2021quantum}, is identical to the game $\game^\ld$ with parameters $\ldparams$ and $\ldc=1$, whose decider is presented in Figure~\ref{fig:ld-decider}. This is because 
   448	\begin{enumerate}
   449	\item The \emph{axis-parallel line-versus-point test} from Figure~\ref{fig:ld-decider} is identical to the \emph{axis-parallel lines test} from~\cite[Figure 1]{ji2021quantum}, with the only difference that in Figure~\ref{fig:ld-decider} the roles of A and B are chosen uniformly at random. This is consistent with the two-prover variant of the tensor code test from~\cite[Section 4.1]{ji2021quantum}.
   450	\item The \emph{diagonal line-versus-point test} from Figure~\ref{fig:ld-decider} is identical to the \emph{subcube commutation test} from~\cite[Figure 1]{ji2021quantum}, with again the added symmetrization between players. 
   451	\item The \emph{consistency test} from Figure~\ref{fig:ld-decider} is identical to the \emph{synchronicity test} from~\cite[Figure 2]{ji2021quantum}.
   452	\end{enumerate}
   453	
   454	As a result,~\cite[Theorem 4.7]{ji2021quantum}, in which we choose the parameter $k$ as $k=m^3d$,  immediately yields \Cref{lem:ld-soundness}.
   455	
   456	To conclude it remains to extend the result to the case of general $\ldc$. This is done 
   457	via a standard reduction, following exactly the same steps as the derivation of Theorem 4.43 from Theorem 4.40 in~\cite{NW19}.
   458	\end{proof}

blueprint/src/chapter/ch13_qpbt_test.tex:15:The classical low individual degree game is a two-player game based on the low individual degree variant of the multilinearity test of Babai, Fortnow, and Lund. In the basic version, one player (the ``points player'') receives a uniformly random point $u \in \F_q^m$ and answers with a value $a \in \F_q$, while the other player (the ``lines player'') receives a random line through $u$ --- either axis-parallel or diagonal --- and answers with a univariate polynomial describing the restriction of a global function to that line. If the players share a polynomial $g\colon \F_q^m \to \F_q$ of individual degree at most $d$ and answer with $g(u)$ and with the restriction $g|_\ell$, they win with probability $1$; the soundness theorem below states that the converse approximately holds. In the simultaneous version, the players' answers are $k$-tuples, checked coordinatewise against a $k$-tuple of low individual degree polynomials.

Informally, the test certifies that the players share the state $\ket{\mathrm{EPR}_q}^{\ot M}$, where $M = 2^m$. On a question of type $(\mathsf{Pauli}, W)$ with $W \in \{X,Z\}$, a player is expected to measure the generalized Pauli basis POVM $\{\tau^W_h\}_{h \in \F_q^M}$ of Chapter~\ref{chap:qpbt-algebra} and report the outcome $h$. Most subtests probe limited information about $h$: given a point $u_W \in \F_q^m$, a player is expected to report the evaluation $g_h(u_W)$ of the low-degree encoding $g_h$ of $h$, and for a fixed basis $W$ these probes are checked against each other by the classical low individual degree game of Section~\ref{sec:ld-verifier}. Consistency \emph{between} the two bases is checked through two-outcome probes: given additionally $r_W \in \F_q$, a player reports $\tr(g_h(u_W)\, r_W) \in \F_2$. The two binary measurements obtained in this way for $W = X$ and $W = Z$ either commute or anticommute, according to the value $\gamma \in \F_2$ of Equation~\eqref{eq:gamma-value} below. When $\gamma = 0$ the verifier checks commutation directly by asking for both bits simultaneously; when $\gamma = 1$ the verifier checks anticommutation by playing the Magic Square game, using Theorem~\ref{thm:ms-from-ac}.

## Findings

- [ ] F1 (changes) `blueprint/src/references.bib:254` — The new paper-gap BibTeX record is missing its closing brace and consumes the following entry.
- [ ] F2 (changes) `MIPStarRE/QPBT/Combining/DirectLowDegree.lean:2` — The new `Transport.Simultaneous` module is absent from the public `DirectLowDegree` facade.
- [ ] F3 (changes) `MIPStarRE/QPBT/Combining/DirectLowDegree/Transport/Consistency/Measurements.lean:152` — Measurement postprocessing functoriality is independently reimplemented in two feature modules instead of the shared measurement API.
- [ ] F4 (changes) `MIPStarRE/QPBT/Games/Sandwich/Support.lean:663` — The sandwich support layer re-proves already available tensor and measurement lemmas instead of reusing shared declarations.

## Review

F1 must be fixed by closing `gap:qpbt_pasting-product-error` with `}` before the next `@techreport`. The blueprint now cites this key at `ch12_qpbt_games.tex:558`, so the malformed bibliography record breaks that cross-reference contract.

F2 leaves all four declarations in `Transport/Simultaneous.lean` outside the aggregate API. `MIPStarRE/QPBT.lean:42` imports only the `DirectLowDegree` facade, and checking `directCoordinateMainFormal` after importing `MIPStarRE.QPBT` produces an unknown-identifier error. Add the simultaneous module to the facade and mention it in the facade documentation.

F3 duplicates the same finite-fiber calculation in `matrixMeasurement_postprocess_comp` and `SandwichInternal.postprocess_postprocess_effect` at `Sandwich/Support.lean:541`. This general result belongs under `MIPStarRE.Quantum.Measurement`; the effect equality should then follow from the shared measurement equality.

F4’s `heteroKron_isProj` is definitionally the already imported `MIPStarRE.LDT.MakingMeasurementsProjective.isProj_kronecker` from `NaimarkCore.lean:59`. Nearby square-summability and projective-fiber lemmas also duplicate private proofs in `DistanceTheorems.lean:364` and `DistanceTheorems/TensorSupport.lean:162,233`. Promote or relocate the common results and reuse them, following the refactor already applied to the finite-sum tensor identities.

The mathematical source audit found no statement drift in `consistencyDefect_sandwich_le`: its hypotheses match `lem:ld-sandwich` at `references/qpbt-paper/06_nonlocal_games_and_mipstar.tex:465-501`, and the explicit factor `8` faithfully instantiates the source’s universal asymptotic constant. The corrected outcome pairing agrees with the cited NEEXP result and the existing paper-gap note.

The retained `exists_pasting_error` admission is clearly marked `**Unfaithful:**`, tied to issue #196, and supported by a valid counterexample in the new paper-gap note. It is therefore a known TODO rather than hidden proof debt. The new sandwich and coordinatewise transport theorems depend only on `propext`, `Classical.choice`, and `Quot.sound`.

Targeted Lean checks for the sandwich, consistency, simultaneous, facade, and GroundSlice modules passed; `git diff --check` also passed. The documented point-reference obstruction remains the principal mathematical residual risk.
